Each trigger schedules ONE coalesced evaluation on the next main turn (`DispatchQueue.main.async`, a pending flag), so the event that met a wait (T's selection, the inspector's rebuild, a sheet's attach) has finished first. A wait is evaluated only after a trigger since its step began — never at its start, so Back stays put. While a Show Me runs, evaluations are held; one runs after its last entry.
82	4. **Conditions (TU-8 (4)).** Baseline at step begin: selection ids, clip-id set, range, latches cleared. `selection`: count in [min, max] and every selected clip matches. `changed`: any clip selected at the step's start differs at any listed path from its start value (`editedProject.json` `clips`, dotted path, absent = `NSNull`, compared with `isEqual`; parsed clips cached per handle). `clips`: at least `added` ids now absent at start (of `kind`). `playhead inside`: start < playhead < end of any clip in the set. `range set`: non-nil; `changed`: that edge differs from start. `sheet`: `window.attachedSheet?.contentViewController is ExportSheetController`. `export_started`/`playing`: latched since step begin (rate ≠ 0). Met → advance in that evaluation.
83	5. **Variables (TU-8 (5)).** `$selection` = start selection; `$created` = ids added by the latest earlier step or earlier call of this Show Me that added any (per step begin the value is recorded; Back restores it); time order = start, ties front track first (`tracks.last` is front). `$time` span = earliest start to latest end; `middle` snapped with `ReelTime.snapToFrame`. `$track` front resolved per call.
84	6. **Navigation and reveal (TU-8 (6)).** Begin a step: baseline, then `inspector.reveal` (`select`, `selectClipSubTab` if offered, scroll; writes no preference); a refusal goes in `reveal_refused`, step still shown. Next only without wait; Skip only optional; Back from step > 1 or finished re-begins the previous step; after the last step `finished`. Each refused with a one-sentence `TutorialRefusal`.
85	7. **Show Me (TU-9).** Entries in order. Tool: resolve variables, `AgentLane.shared.submit(tool:argumentsJSON:document:askFirst:completion:)` pinned to the runner's document, `askFirst` answering `true` (the press is the ask), completion hopped to main (`DispatchQueue.main.async`; dropped if the runner was replaced). `isError` → stop, `error` = its text verbatim. Menu: `UIMenu.lookup` for the editor's window; missing → "The menu bar has no A ▸ B ▸ C."; no target or `isEnabled` false → "A ▸ B ▸ C is not available now."; else `UIMenu.perform` (its undo grouping); unhandled → "A ▸ B ▸ C was not handled." A failed Show Me leaves the step. Earlier entries' edits stay, each an ordinary undo step.
86	8. **Dev tools.** `AgentServer+Tutorials.swift`: `target(a)`; no editor window refused as `select_inspector_tab` does; unknown id refused naming `TutorialLibrary.ids`; a refused id answers the model's reason. `tutorial_step show_me`: `onMain { runner.showMe() }`, then `AgentLane.shared.releasingLock` polling `showMeRunning` on main every 50 ms up to 60 s (the assistant tools' precedent), then the state.
87	9. **Inspector move.** Pure move first, then `visible_sections` (ids whose frame intersects the clip view's visible rect, top to bottom) in the dev tool's answer.
88	10. **Checker.** Probe arg 4 is `{"guide": <extracted guide>, "mutants": {name: <document>}}`; answer `model: {guide: {id: null|reason}, mutants: {name: null|reason}}` and `filter_number_matches` (a practice clip's `matches` on JSON `{"has_sound": 1}`). Problems: a checker-accepted tutorial the model refused; a model mutant decoded; `filter_number_matches` true; empty/missing practice `media` (nit 2); a menu Show Me whose verdict is `modal`/`framework`. `MODEL_MUTANTS` = `unknown-spotlight`, `section-not-in-table`, `section-other-home`, `unknown-variable` plus new MUTANTS `unknown-step-key`, `selection-min-negative`, `range-both`, `sheet-other`, `optional-not-bool`, `kind-unknown`, built from the fixture page; the selftest also requires `check()` to refuse each. New selftest cases: those six, `model-guide-refused`, `model-mutant-accepted`, `filter-number`, `practice-media-empty`, `menu-verdict-modal`. The fixture CONTROL must decode in the real model.
89	11. **Proof `tutorial_proof.py <dir>/agent.sock`.** Each run on a fresh `new_project {practice: true}` closed with `close_project {discard: true}` (front document only). Rows: T1 log clean. P-<id> per tutorial as a person, after each action the step read and, on a reveal, `select_inspector_tab {}`'s tab, sub_tab and `visible_sections`: volume (`set_selection` Dawn, `set_audio` 0.5, `play_preview {seconds: 1}`); split (`set_selection` Dawn, `set_playhead` 3 s, `perform_menu_item` Clip ▸ Split); add_title (`add_track`, `add_text_clip` — still step 1 — `set_selection`, `set_text`, `set_video`); cross_dissolve (`set_selection` Sea, `perform_menu_item` Clip ▸ Transition ▸ Cross Dissolve, `set_transition_duration`); export (`set_range` start then end, `perform_menu_item` File ▸ Export…, `next`, `export` to `work/tutorial_proof/`, wait done, `cancel_sheet`). M-<id> by Show Me alone (show_me, else next, else skip), then `get_project`: Dawn volume 1.5; four clips, Dawn split at 3 s; a second track with a text clip "My first title" at y 300; Sea's `transition_in` cross dissolve, start moved; range [0, 3 s]. The export Show Me writes `~/Movies/Frame Job Tutorial.mp4`: the row FAILS without running if that file exists, waits for the export (id from `last_show_me.results`), then deletes only the file it made. C-<id> on `new_project {}`: four exact needs sentences; add_title starts, then exit. B1 Back stays put; S1 Skip; N1 Next refused on a wait step; E1 Exit leaves project and undo untouched; R1 refused tool Show Me (split step 3 after `set_playhead` 15 s: step stays, error non-empty, three clips); R2 greyed menu (cross_dissolve step 2 after `set_selection []`: exact sentence, no transition); U1 `undo` after the volume Show Me restores the volume, step stays 3, `redo` reapplies. `Rows <ID> pass|fail — <detail>`, then `scores:`; exit 0 iff none failed.

## Interfaces
```swift
enum TutorialJSON { static func isBool(_ v: Any) -> Bool; static func isInt(_ v: Any) -> Bool }  // isInt: NSNumber, not CFBoolean, integral
struct TutorialModelError: LocalizedError { let message: String }
struct TutorialLibrary {
    let pages: [TutorialPage]; let refused: [String: String]      // tutorial id → the model's reason
    static func decode(_ data: Data) throws -> TutorialLibrary     // throws on top level (not an object, format != 1, pages not a list)
    static func bundled() throws -> TutorialLibrary                // Bundle.main "Tutorials.json", memoised
    func tutorial(id: String) -> Tutorial?; var ids: [String] { get }   // guide order
}
struct TutorialPage { let page: String; let title: String; let tutorials: [Tutorial] }
struct Tutorial { let id, title, anchor: String; let needs: [String: Any]?; let steps: [TutorialStep] }
struct TutorialStep { let text: String; let reveal: TutorialReveal?; let spotlight: String?
    let wait: [TutorialCondition]; let showMe: [TutorialShowMe]; let optional: Bool }
struct TutorialReveal: Equatable { let tab: InspectorTab; let subTab: ClipSubTab?; let section: String? }
enum TutorialClipSet: String { case selection = "$selection", created = "$created" }
enum TutorialRangeEdge: String { case start, end }
enum TutorialCondition { case selection(min: Int, max: Int?, filter: [String: Any]), changed([String]),
    clips(added: Int, kind: String?), playheadInside(TutorialClipSet), rangeSet, rangeChanged(TutorialRangeEdge),
    sheetExport, exportStarted, playing }
enum TutorialShowMe { case tool(name: String, args: [String: Any]), menu(path: [String]) }

struct TutorialRefusal: Error { let sentence: String }
enum TutorialAdvance: String { case wait, next, skip }
struct TutorialShowMeOutcome { let step: Int; let ok: Bool; let error: String?; let results: [String] }  // results: each call's result text
final class TutorialRunner {
    static func start(_ tutorial: Tutorial, in editor: EditorViewController) throws -> TutorialRunner  // TutorialRefusal; installs, replacing
    func trigger(); func documentDidChange(isLive: Bool); func playbackRateChanged(_ rate: Float); func noteExportStarted()
    func next() throws; func back() throws; func skip() throws; func showMe() throws; func exit()   // TutorialRefusal
    var showMeRunning: Bool { get }; var offers: [String] { get }; func state() -> [String: Any]
}
struct TutorialBaseline { init(document: ProjectDocument) }   // selection (time-ordered), clip ids, range, per-path values
enum TutorialWait { static func needsSentence(_ needs: [String: Any]?, in snapshot: ProjectSnapshot) -> String? }
enum TutorialVariables { static func resolve(_ value: Any, selection: [UInt32], created: [UInt32],
    snapshot: ProjectSnapshot, playhead: Ticks) throws -> Any }   // TutorialRefusal
```

Dev tools (each also takes `project`, injected by `tool()`): `tutorial_start {id}` (main), `tutorial_state {}` (main), `tutorial_step {action: "show_me"|"next"|"back"|"skip"}` (off main), `tutorial_exit {}` (main). Every answer but a refusal is the state: `{ok, project, running}`, and when running also `id, title, step` (1-based), `steps, text, optional, wait` (bool), `show_me` (bool), `offers` (subset of `back, show_me, skip, next, exit` in that order), `spotlight, reveal` (`{tab, sub_tab, section}` or null), `reveal_refused, finished, show_me_running, last_show_me` (`{step, ok, error, results}` or null), `selection_at_start, created, completed` (`[{step, by}]`).

## Approach
1. **Model (TU-8 (1)).** Decode format 1; refuse per tutorial (into `refused`) any key, type or value outside TU-2 (2)–(9) — closed keys at every level, id pattern, filter keys/kinds, `min`/`max`, `range` exactly one, `sheet` "export", `true` literals, `reveal` against `InspectorTab`/`ClipSubTab`/`TutorialTargets.sections` homes, `spotlight` against `TutorialTargets`, show_me shape, `$`-strings/keys. Catalog, menu-bar, inventory and fixture-path checks stay the checker's (build time); one failing at run time is a refused Show Me.
2. **Start (TU-8 (2)).** One runner per editor window, `editor.tutorialRunner`; start replaces; Exit sets it nil and undoes nothing; closing the window ends it. Needs are checked against `document.editedProject.snapshot` with `TutorialClipFacts`; unmet → `TutorialRefusal(needsSentence)`: `This tutorial needs ` + (`a clip` | `a`/`an` `<kind> clip`) + (none | ` that ` + predicates) + `.`; predicates in `TutorialClipFacts.keys` order: `has sound`/`has no sound`, `has a picture`/`has no picture`, `meets the clip before it on its track`/`does not meet the clip before it on its track`, `has a transition in`/`has no transition in`; joined `p`, `p1 and p2`, `p1, p2 and p3`. E.g. "This tutorial needs a clip that has sound."
3. **Triggers (TU-8 (3)).** Committed document change and `viewStateDidChange` (the editor's hook; `isLive` ticks ignored), playhead moves, rate changes, `NSWindow.willBeginSheetNotification`/`didEndSheetNotification` on the editor's window (block observers removed in `deinit`), and `noteExportStarted`. No polling. The inspector tab is no trigger: no condition reads it. Each trigger schedules ONE coalesced evaluation on the next main turn (`DispatchQueue.main.async`, a pending flag), so the event that met a wait (T's selection, the inspector's rebuild, a sheet's attach) has finished first. A wait is evaluated only after a trigger since its step began — never at its start, so Back stays put. While a Show Me runs, evaluations are held; one runs after its last entry.
4. **Conditions (TU-8 (4)).** Baseline at step begin: selection ids, clip-id set, range, latches cleared. `selection`: count in [min, max] and every selected clip matches. `changed`: any clip selected at the step's start differs at any listed path from its start value (`editedProject.json` `clips`, dotted path, absent = `NSNull`, compared with `isEqual`; parsed clips cached per handle). `clips`: at least `added` ids now absent at start (of `kind`). `playhead inside`: start < playhead < end of any clip in the set. `range set`: non-nil; `changed`: that edge differs from start. `sheet`: `window.attachedSheet?.contentViewController is ExportSheetController`. `export_started`/`playing`: latched since step begin (rate ≠ 0). Met → advance in that evaluation.
5. **Variables (TU-8 (5)).** `$selection` = start selection; `$created` = ids added by the latest earlier step or earlier call of this Show Me that added any (per step begin the value is recorded; Back restores it); time order = start, ties front track first (`tracks.last` is front). `$time` span = earliest start to latest end; `middle` snapped with `ReelTime.snapToFrame`. `$track` front resolved per call.
6. **Navigation and reveal (TU-8 (6)).** Begin a step: baseline, then `inspector.reveal` (`select`, `selectClipSubTab` if offered, scroll; writes no preference); a refusal goes in `reveal_refused`, step still shown. Next only without wait; Skip only optional; Back from step > 1 or finished re-begins the previous step; after the last step `finished`. Each refused with a one-sentence `TutorialRefusal`.
7. **Show Me (TU-9).** Entries in order. Tool: resolve variables, `AgentLane.shared.submit(tool:argumentsJSON:document:askFirst:completion:)` pinned to the runner's document, `askFirst` answering `true` (the press is the ask), completion hopped to main (`DispatchQueue.main.async`; dropped if the runner was replaced). `isError` → stop, `error` = its text verbatim. Menu: `UIMenu.lookup` for the editor's window; missing → "The menu bar has no A ▸ B ▸ C."; no target or `isEnabled` false → "A ▸ B ▸ C is not available now."; else `UIMenu.perform` (its undo grouping); unhandled → "A ▸ B ▸ C was not handled." A failed Show Me leaves the step. Earlier entries' edits stay, each an ordinary undo step.
8. **Dev tools.** `AgentServer+Tutorials.swift`: `target(a)`; no editor window refused as `select_inspector_tab` does; unknown id refused naming `TutorialLibrary.ids`; a refused id answers the model's reason. `tutorial_step show_me`: `onMain { runner.showMe() }`, then `AgentLane.shared.releasingLock` polling `showMeRunning` on main every 50 ms up to 60 s (the assistant tools' precedent), then the state.
9. **Inspector move.** Pure move first, then `visible_sections` (ids whose frame intersects the clip view's visible rect, top to bottom) in the dev tool's answer.
10. **Checker.** Probe arg 4 is `{"guide": <extracted guide>, "mutants": {name: <document>}}`; answer `model: {guide: {id: null|reason}, mutants: {name: null|reason}}` and `filter_number_matches` (a practice clip's `matches` on JSON `{"has_sound": 1}`). Problems: a checker-accepted tutorial the model refused; a model mutant decoded; `filter_number_matches` true; empty/missing practice `media` (nit 2); a menu Show Me whose verdict is `modal`/`framework`. `MODEL_MUTANTS` = `unknown-spotlight`, `section-not-in-table`, `section-other-home`, `unknown-variable` plus new MUTANTS `unknown-step-key`, `selection-min-negative`, `range-both`, `sheet-other`, `optional-not-bool`, `kind-unknown`, built from the fixture page; the selftest also requires `check()` to refuse each. New selftest cases: those six, `model-guide-refused`, `model-mutant-accepted`, `filter-number`, `practice-media-empty`, `menu-verdict-modal`. The fixture CONTROL must decode in the real model.
11. **Proof `tutorial_proof.py <dir>/agent.sock`.** Each run on a fresh `new_project {practice: true}` closed with `close_project {discard: true}` (front document only). Rows: T1 log clean. P-<id> per tutorial as a person, after each action the step read and, on a reveal, `select_inspector_tab {}`'s tab, sub_tab and `visible_sections`: volume (`set_selection` Dawn, `set_audio` 0.5, `play_preview {seconds: 1}`); split (`set_selection` Dawn, `set_playhead` 3 s, `perform_menu_item` Clip ▸ Split); add_title (`add_track`, `add_text_clip` — still step 1 — `set_selection`, `set_text`, `set_video`); cross_dissolve (`set_selection` Sea, `perform_menu_item` Clip ▸ Transition ▸ Cross Dissolve, `set_transition_duration`); export (`set_range` start then end, `perform_menu_item` File ▸ Export…, `next`, `export` to `work/tutorial_proof/`, wait done, `cancel_sheet`). M-<id> by Show Me alone (show_me, else next, else skip), then `get_project`: Dawn volume 1.5; four clips, Dawn split at 3 s; a second track with a text clip "My first title" at y 300; Sea's `transition_in` cross dissolve, start moved; range [0, 3 s]. The export Show Me writes `~/Movies/Frame Job Tutorial.mp4`: the row FAILS without running if that file exists, waits for the export (id from `last_show_me.results`), then deletes only the file it made. C-<id> on `new_project {}`: four exact needs sentences; add_title starts, then exit. B1 Back stays put; S1 Skip; N1 Next refused on a wait step; E1 Exit leaves project and undo untouched; R1 refused tool Show Me (split step 3 after `set_playhead` 15 s: step stays, error non-empty, three clips); R2 greyed menu (cross_dissolve step 2 after `set_selection []`: exact sentence, no transition); U1 `undo` after the volume Show Me restores the volume, step stays 3, `redo` reapplies. `Rows <ID> pass|fail — <detail>`, then `scores:`; exit 0 iff none failed.
12. **Mutants (7)**, run once at the end: evaluate at step begin (B1); no Show Me hold (M-canvas.add_title); menu skips `isEnabled` (R2); `askFirst` false (M-export.range); failed Show Me advances (R1); needs unchecked (C rows); `AgentServer+Export` hook removed (P-export.range). Nit 3 has no instrument; stated in the record.

## Constraints
- `EditorViewController.swift` is frozen: the three wiring lines only. `AgentServer.swift` untouched (DevTools merges). New files ≤400 lines; `+Inspector` is 403, under 600.
- Dev tools follow `AgentServer+InspectorTab.swift`/`+Assistant.swift`; rows sit before `import_media` in `dev_tools.py` order (`op_argument_proof.py`, `assistant_session_proof.py` A0). `AssistantToolTable` withholds them via `devToolNames`.
- Undo: no `registerUndo` outside `ProjectDocument`; tool edits through the lane's `performGroupedEdit`, menu edits through `UIMenu.perform` → `inUndoGroupIfRegistered`. Never `flush` the undo manager.
- Never take the lane lock on main (`AgentLane.swift` header); the product Show Me never blocks main.
- Hygiene: no `!`/`as!`/`try!`; `[weak self]`; no `async`; the runner's two main hops are a new documented seam (CLAUDE.md edit owed). No log line starting `Frame Job: `.
- `TutorialTargets.swift` stays the target table; `TutorialClipFacts` answers every filter. `tutorial_extract.py` is the only parser.
- The guide edit must keep `tutorial_check: 5 tutorials, 17 steps, 0 problems`.
- Proofs never perform a persisting View item; the instance is the proof's own, killed by its pid.

## Verification
Targeted (run while iterating; covers only the code in **Files**):
```
python3 tools/proof/tutorial_check.py --selftest
python3 tools/proof/tutorial_check.py
make typecheck                                   # seconds; 0 errors, the 4 baseline warnings
make app-debug && python3 tools/proof/proof_app.py launch
python3 tools/proof/tutorial_proof.py <dir>/agent.sock
python3 tools/proof/v3_tools.py                   # select_inspector_tab after the move
python3 tools/proof/v2_menu.py <dir>/agent.sock   # UIMenu's flag narrowed
```
Full (run once, after the targeted checks pass; only commands the files in **Files** can affect):
```
make gate                                        # ~245 s last run (test 125 s, app 109 s)
RC_PROOF_APP=release python3 tools/proof/tutorial_proof.py <dir>/agent.sock   # covers: the runner, Show Me, dev tools
RC_PROOF_APP=release python3 tools/proof/v2_menu.py <dir>/agent.sock          # covers: menu delivery compiled in every build
RC_PROOF_APP=release python3 tools/proof/v3_tools.py                          # covers: select_inspector_tab's move and visible_sections
RC_PROOF_APP=release python3 tools/proof/op_argument_proof.py <dir>/agent.sock # covers: the dev-tool block and marker count
RC_PROOF_APP=release python3 tools/proof/assistant_session_proof.py           # covers: A0's dev-tool count
```
Passing means: `make gate` prints `gate: PASS`; `grep "Frame Job: " <dir>/framejob.log` prints nothing; every proof exits 0 with no failed row; the selftest passes CONTROL and every mutant; each of the 7 mutants fails its named row.

## Out of scope
- TU3: the coach panel, the spotlight window and resolving target names to views, Help ▸ Tutorials ▸ per-page items, export-sheet ids, `snapshot_ui`'s panel kind, the practice-project offer, the guide's tutorials page, `menus-and-shortcuts.md`, manual-check rows.
- Auto-play/videos, `framejob://` links, rolling tutorials out to more pages.
- Any op, `rc_*` export, format bump or product tool.

## CLAUDE.md edits owed
- Root `CLAUDE.md` "Verifying a build": the dev-tool list gains `tutorial_start`, `tutorial_state`, `tutorial_step`, `tutorial_exit`.
- `app/CLAUDE.md` Tutorials: entries for `TutorialModel`, `TutorialRunner`, `TutorialWait`, `TutorialVariables`, `TutorialShowMe`; `TutorialClipFacts` read by the runner. Inspector: `InspectorReveal.swift`. Agent: `AgentServer+Tutorials.swift`; DevTools table lists the four. `UIMenu.swift`: delivery compiled in every build. Hygiene: the runner's evaluation hop and Show Me completion hop as `DispatchQueue.main.async` seams.

## Owner choices
- Show Me answers the lane's ask-first itself, so Export a range's Show Me writes `~/Movies/Frame Job Tutorial.mp4` without asking. Recommendation: keep (pressing Show Me is the ask); TU3 may show the path in the panel.

You are trying to find real problems with a spec before anyone writes code. You get one round. There is no back-and-forth.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

## blender
You have access to Blender tools to interact with a Blender scene directly.
Blender must be running with the MCP add-on enabled and connected.

IMPORTANT: Respect existing structure and naming conventions.
NEVER assume missing values - inspect the scene first.
Do not destructively modify objects without confirmation.

# Bundled Manuals

Reference documentation is bundled alongside this server as plain-text RST files.
Search and read them directly with standard text tools (grep, file read, etc.):
  * `data/api/` - Blender Python API reference (RST files per module/class).
    Consult when writing or debugging `bpy` code: operator signatures, type
    properties, enum values, etc.
  * `data/manual/` - Blender user manual (RST files mirroring the official manual structure).
    Consult for conceptual explanations, workflow guidance, and feature overviews.

# Executing Code

The `execute_blender_code` tool runs Python code via `bpy` in the connected Blender instance.

The `execute_blender_code` tool is a last resort, if there are other tools that provide
the functionality you need, use those instead.

Prefer operators (`bpy.ops`) for standard actions (adding primitives, applying modifiers,
setting origins) - they handle defaults and context. Use the data API (`bpy.data`) for
precise control or to avoid side effects.

Many operators depend on the current mode (Object, Edit, Sculpt, etc.) and which objects
are active/selected. Verify or set the mode first - wrong mode either fails or silently
does nothing.

The **active object** and **selection** are distinct. Many operators require both.
Set them explicitly - do not assume the current state. Operators change selection and
active state as a side effect, so re-set both between sequential operator calls on
different objects.

Update the dependency graph after changes before reading computed properties
(world matrices, modifier results, etc.).

In edit mode, access mesh geometry through the bmesh API, not the regular mesh data API.
Flush bmesh changes back to the mesh - forgetting this silently loses all edits.

Return structured data (dicts, lists) from executed code, not print output.

# Scene & Data Structure

Blender uses a datablock system - objects and their underlying data (meshes, materials,
cameras, etc.) are separate entities.

Hierarchy:
  * **Scene** - top-level container. A .blend can have multiple.
  * **View Layer** - controls collection visibility/selectability.
  * **Collection** - organizational tree. Objects live in collections; can be nested;
    objects can belong to multiple collections.
  * **Object** - has a transform (location, rotation, scale) and references underlying data
    (Mesh, Curve, Camera, etc.). Multiple objects can share the same data (linked duplicates).
  * **Datablocks** - the actual data: geometry, materials, textures, etc.

Key concepts:
  * Objects and data are separate - deleting one does not delete the other.
  * Orphaned datablocks (zero users) are purged on save/reload or manual purge.
  * Objects created via the data API must be linked to a collection to appear in a scene.
  * Shared data: check user count before modifying a datablock - editing a shared mesh
    affects all objects referencing it. Make single-user first if needed.
  * In most cases file assets:
    * Images, Fonts, Sounds, other `.blend` files -  corraspond to a data-block.

Visibility has three independent states:
  * **Viewport hidden** - still fully scriptable.
  * **Disabled in view layer** - excluded; may be inaccessible to view-layer-dependent operators.
  * **Disabled for render** - skipped during render, otherwise normal.
Check these when objects seem "missing" or operators skip them.

Blender defaults to meters. Check scene unit settings before creating dimensioned objects.

Exploring scenes:
  * Walk the collection hierarchy for an overview first.
  * Don't dump entire scenes - inspect progressively for large scenes.
  * Check object types, parenting, modifiers, and materials before making changes.

# Object Types & Creation

Object types: Mesh, Curve, Su… [truncated]

Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>

<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>

<?claude block s1?>

<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

38	## Interfaces
39	```swift
40	enum TutorialJSON { static func isBool(_ v: Any) -> Bool; static func isInt(_ v: Any) -> Bool }  // isInt: NSNumber, not CFBoolean, integral
41	struct TutorialModelError: LocalizedError { let message: String }
42	struct TutorialLibrary {
43	    let pages: [TutorialPage]; let refused: [String: String]      // tutorial id → the model's reason
44	    static func decode(_ data: Data) throws -> TutorialLibrary     // throws on top level (not an object, format != 1, pages not a list)
45	    static func bundled() throws -> TutorialLibrary                // Bundle.main "Tutorials.json", memoised
46	    func tutorial(id: String) -> Tutorial?; var ids: [String] { get }   // guide order
47	}
48	struct TutorialPage { let page: String; let title: String; let tutorials: [Tutorial] }
49	struct Tutorial { let id, title, anchor: String; let needs: [String: Any]?; let steps: [TutorialStep] }
50	struct TutorialStep { let text: String; let reveal: TutorialReveal?; let spotlight: String?
51	    let wait: [TutorialCondition]; let showMe: [TutorialShowMe]; let optional: Bool }
52	struct TutorialReveal: Equatable { let tab: InspectorTab; let subTab: ClipSubTab?; let section: String? }
53	enum TutorialClipSet: String { case selection = "$selection", created = "$created" }
54	enum TutorialRangeEdge: String { case start, end }
55	enum TutorialCondition { case selection(min: Int, max: Int?, filter: [String: Any]), changed([String]),
56	    clips(added: Int, kind: String?), playheadInside(TutorialClipSet), rangeSet, rangeChanged(TutorialRangeEdge),
57	    sheetExport, exportStarted, playing }
58	enum TutorialShowMe { case tool(name: String, args: [String: Any]), menu(path: [String]) }
59	
60	struct TutorialRefusal: Error { let sentence: String }
61	enum TutorialAdvance: String { case wait, next, skip }
62	struct TutorialShowMeOutcome { let step: Int; let ok: Bool; let error: String?; let results: [String] }  // results: each call's result text
63	final class TutorialRunner {
64	    static func start(_ tutorial: Tutorial, in editor: EditorViewController) throws -> TutorialRunner  // TutorialRefusal; installs, replacing
65	    func trigger(); func documentDidChange(isLive: Bool); func playbackRateChanged(_ rate: Float); func noteExportStarted()
66	    func next() throws; func back() throws; func skip() throws; func showMe() throws; func exit()   // TutorialRefusal
67	    var showMeRunning: Bool { get }; var offers: [String] { get }; func state() -> [String: Any]
68	}
69	struct TutorialBaseline { init(document: ProjectDocument) }   // selection (time-ordered), clip ids, range, per-path values
70	enum TutorialWait { static func needsSentence(_ needs: [String: Any]?, in snapshot: ProjectSnapshot) -> String? }
71	enum TutorialVariables { static func resolve(_ value: Any, selection: [UInt32], created: [UInt32],
72	    snapshot: ProjectSnapshot, playhead: Ticks) throws -> Any }   // TutorialRefusal
73	extension InspectorViewController { func reveal(_ r: TutorialReveal) -> String?   // nil, or the refusal sentence
74	    func visibleSectionIDs() -> [String] }
75	```
76	Dev tools (each also takes `project`, injected by `tool()`): `tutorial_start {id}` (main), `tutorial_state {}` (main), `tutorial_step {action: "show_me"|"next"|"back"|"skip"}` (off main), `tutorial_exit {}` (main). Every answer but a refusal is the state: `{ok, project, running}`, and when running also `id, title, step` (1-based), `steps, text, optional, wait` (bool), `show_me` (bool), `offers` (subset of `back, show_me, skip, next, exit` in that order), `spotlight, reveal` (`{tab, sub_tab, section}` or null), `reveal_refused, finished, show_me_running, last_show_me` (`{step, ok, error, results}` or null), `selection_at_start, created, completed` (`[{step, by}]`).
77	
78	## Approach
79	1. **Model (TU-8 (1)).** Decode format 1; refuse per tutorial (into `refused`) any key, type or value outside TU-2 (2)–(9) — closed keys at every level, id pattern, filter keys/kinds, `min`/`max`, `range` exactly one, `sheet` "export", `true` literals, `reveal` against `InspectorTab`/`ClipSubTab`/`TutorialTargets.sections` homes, `spotlight` against `TutorialTargets`, show_me shape, `$`-strings/keys. Catalog, menu-bar, inventory and fixture-path checks stay the checker's (build time); one failing at run time is a refused Show Me.
80	2. **Start (TU-8 (2)).** One runner per editor window, `editor.tutorialRunner`; start replaces; Exit sets it nil and undoes nothing; closing the window ends it. Needs are checked against `document.editedProject.snapshot` with `TutorialClipFacts`; unmet → `TutorialRefusal(needsSentence)`: `This tutorial needs ` + (`a clip` | `a`/`an` `<kind> clip`) + (none | ` that ` + predicates) + `.`; predicates in `TutorialClipFacts.keys` order: `has sound`/`has no sound`, `has a picture`/`has no picture`, `meets the clip before it on its track`/`does not meet the clip before it on its track`, `has a transition in`/`has no transition in`; joined `p`, `p1 and p2`, `p1, p2 and p3`. E.g. "This tutorial needs a clip that has sound."
81	3. **Triggers (TU-8 (3)).** Committed document change and `viewStateDidChange` (the editor's hook; `isLive` ticks ignored), playhead moves, rate changes, `NSWindow.willBeginSheetNotification`/`didEndSheetNotification` on the editor's window (block observers removed in `deinit`), and `noteExportStarted`. No polling. The inspector tab is no trigger: no condition reads it. Each trigger schedules ONE coalesced evaluation on the next main turn (`DispatchQueue.main.async`, a pending flag), so the event that met a wait (T's selection, the inspector's rebuild, a sheet's attach) has finished first. A wait is evaluated only after a trigger since its step began — never at its start, so Back stays put. While a Show Me runs, evaluations are held; one runs after its last entry.
82	4. **Conditions (TU-8 (4)).** Baseline at step begin: selection ids, clip-id set, range, latches cleared. `selection`: count in [min, max] and every selected clip matches. `changed`: any clip selected at the step's start differs at any listed path from its start value (`editedProject.json` `clips`, dotted path, absent = `NSNull`, compared with `isEqual`; parsed clips cached per handle). `clips`: at least `added` ids now absent at start (of `kind`). `playhead inside`: start < playhead < end of any clip in the set. `range set`: non-nil; `changed`: that edge differs from start. `sheet`: `window.attachedSheet?.contentViewController is ExportSheetController`. `export_started`/`playing`: latched since step begin (rate ≠ 0). Met → advance in that evaluation.
83	5. **Variables (TU-8 (5)).** `$selection` = start selection; `$created` = ids added by the latest earlier step or earlier call of this Show Me that added any (per step begin the value is recorded; Back restores it); time order = start, ties front track first (`tracks.last` is front). `$time` span = earliest start to latest end; `middle` snapped with `ReelTime.snapToFrame`. `$track` front resolved per call.
84	6. **Navigation and reveal (TU-8 (6)).** Begin a step: baseline, then `inspector.reveal` (`select`, `selectClipSubTab` if offered, scroll; writes no preference); a refusal goes in `reveal_refused`, step still shown. Next only without wait; Skip only optional; Back from step > 1 or finished re-begins the previous step; after the last step `finished`. Each refused with a one-sentence `TutorialRefusal`.
85	7. **Show Me (TU-9).** Entries in order. Tool: resolve variables, `AgentLane.shared.submit(tool:argumentsJSON:document:askFirst:completion:)` pinned to the runner's document, `askFirst` answering `true` (the press is the ask), completion hopped to main (`DispatchQueue.main.async`; dropped if the runner was replaced). `isError` → stop, `error` = its text verbatim. A failed Show Me leaves the step. Earlier entries' edits stay, each an ordinary undo step.

# MCP Server Instructions

The following MCP servers have provided instructions for how to use their tools and resources:

## blender
You have access to Blender tools to interact with a Blender scene directly.
Blender must be running with the MCP add-on enabled and connected.

IMPORTANT: Respect existing structure and naming conventions.
NEVER assume missing values - inspect the scene first.
Do not destructively modify objects without confirmation.

# Bundled Manuals

Reference documentation is bundled alongside this server as plain-text RST files.
Search and read them directly with standard text tools (grep, file read, etc.):
  * `data/api/` - Blender Python API reference (RST files per module/class).
    Consult when writing or debugging `bpy` code: operator signatures, type
    properties, enum values, etc.
  * `data/manual/` - Blender user manual (RST files mirroring the official manual structure).
    Consult for conceptual explanations, workflow guidance, and feature overviews.

# Executing Code

The `execute_blender_code` tool runs Python code via `bpy` in the connected Blender instance.

The `execute_blender_code` tool is a last resort, if there are other tools that provide
the functionality you need, use those instead.

Prefer operators (`bpy.ops`) for standard actions (adding primitives, applying modifiers,
setting origins) - they handle defaults and context. Use the data API (`bpy.data`) for
precise control or to avoid side effects.

Many operators depend on the current mode (Object, Edit, Sculpt, etc.) and which objects
are active/selected. Verify or set the mode first - wrong mode either fails or silently
does nothing.

The **active object** and **selection** are distinct. Many operators require both.
Set them explicitly - do not assume the current state. Operators change selection and
active state as a side effect, so re-set both between sequential operator calls on
different objects.

Update the dependency graph after changes before reading computed properties
(world matrices, modifier results, etc.).

In edit mode, access mesh geometry through the bmesh API, not the regular mesh data API.
Flush bmesh changes back to the mesh - forgetting this silently loses all edits.

Return structured data (dicts, lists) from executed code, not print output.

# Scene & Data Structure

Blender uses a datablock system - objects and their underlying data (meshes, materials,
cameras, etc.) are separate entities.

Hierarchy:
  * **Scene** - top-level container. A .blend can have multiple.
  * **View Layer** - controls collection visibility/selectability.
  * **Collection** - organizational tree. Objects live in collections; can be nested;
    objects can belong to multiple collections.
  * **Object** - has a transform (location, rotation, scale) and references underlying data
    (Mesh, Curve, Camera, etc.). Multiple objects can share the same data (linked duplicates).
  * **Datablocks** - the actual data: geometry, materials, textures, etc.

Key concepts:
  * Objects and data are separate - deleting one does not delete the other.
  * Orphaned datablocks (zero users) are purged on save/reload or manual purge.
  * Objects created via the data API must be linked to a collection to appear in a scene.
  * Shared data: check user count before modifying a datablock - editing a shared mesh
    affects all objects referencing it. Make single-user first if needed.
  * In most cases file assets:
    * Images, Fonts, Sounds, other `.blend` files -  corraspond to a data-block.

Visibility has three independent states:
  * **Viewport hidden** - still fully scriptable.
  * **Disabled in view layer** - excluded; may be inaccessible to view-layer-dependent operators.
  * **Disabled for render** - skipped during render, otherwise normal.
Check these when objects seem "missing" or operators skip them.

Blender defaults to meters. Check scene unit settings before creating dimensioned objects.

Exploring scenes:
  * Walk the collection hierarchy for an overview first.
  * Don't dump entire scenes - inspect progressively for large scenes.
  * Check object types, parenting, modifiers, and materials before making changes.

# Object Types & Creation

Object types: Mesh, Curve, Su… [truncated]

## claude.ai Claude Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>\n\n<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>\n\n<?claude block s1?>\n\n<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

While auto mode is active:

You can do much of your work through the Bash tool when it is the simpler route: read files with cat, head, or sed -n, search with grep and find, and make small, mechanical file changes with sed, heredocs, or short scripts instead of the dedicated Read, Edit, or Write tools. The choice is yours: prefer Edit or Write when a shell edit would be fragile, such as exact or multi-line replacements, or sed/awk flags that differ between GNU and BSD/macOS.

1	# Spec §11 — decisions: Tutorials (road map "tutorials")
2	
3	Part of spec §11, *Decisions made — do not re-litigate*. The index of every decision is
4	[`README.md`](README.md).
5	
6	The road map that makes these is in progress: `designs/tutorials.md` (TU0–TU4), whose
7	"Record" section holds each phase's record. TU-1..TU-6 were recorded in TU0, before any code;
8	TU-2's vocabulary was settled in TU1 and is normative here, not in the road map. TU-7 was recorded in
9	TU1b, before its code. The owner's
10	answers of 2026-10-31 (the road map's §10) are marked "owner": the five model tutorials kept,
11	a bundled practice project built now, and the word "Tutorials".
12	
13	- **TU-1 — One source: a tutorial is an ordinary numbered list in its feature's guide page,
14	  and its machine half is an HTML comment at the end of each item.** The sentence a reader
15	  follows on GitHub is the sentence the app shows, word for word, because both are the same
16	  lines; no second set of docs is started, and a tutorial cannot drift from its page. A
17	  heading `### Tutorial: <title>` opens one, and a `<!-- tutorial {json} -->` line under it
18	  names it. Every Markdown viewer hides the comments, so a reader sees plain steps.
19	  `tools/tutorials/tutorial_extract.py` reads every page of `docs/guide/` and the app build's
20	  "Write Tutorials" step writes its output into the bundle as `Tutorials.json`:
21	  `{"format": 1, "pages": [{"page", "title" (the page's H1), "tutorials": [{"id", "title",
22	  "anchor" (the heading's GitHub slug), "needs" (default `{}`), "steps": [{"text", …the
23	  step's machine-half keys verbatim}]}]}]}`, pages sorted by file name, only pages that hold
24	  a tutorial, `json.dumps(indent=1, ensure_ascii=False)`. The extractor refuses a page whose
25	  tutorial breaks the structure of TU-2 (1), naming the page and the line, and the build
26	  fails. Risk accepted: a tutorial's words are the guide's register, written for a reader of
27	  the page, and the coach panel shows them as they are.
28	- **TU-2 — The step vocabulary is closed, and `tools/proof/tutorial_check.py` in `make test`
29	  refuses anything outside it, naming the page, the tutorial and the step.** The vocabulary:
30	  1. *Structure.* A heading `### Tutorial: <title>`; its next non-blank line starts
31	     `<!-- tutorial {json} -->`; then the first ordered list, numbered 1..n; an item's
32	     continuation lines are indented at least 3 spaces; an item may end with
33	     `<!-- step {json} -->` (the JSON may span lines), and nothing follows `-->` in the
34	     item; no `<!-- tutorial` or `<!-- step` appears anywhere else in the page. The step's
35	     sentence is the item's text less the comment, its lines joined by one space; it is
36	     never empty, and its Markdown is kept.
37	  2. *Tutorial keys.* `id`, required, matching `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*(\.[a-z][a-z0-9_]*)+$` and
38	     unique across the guide; `needs`, optional, `{"clip": <filter>}`.
39	  3. *Clip filter.* Optional `has_sound` (bool: the clip has an `audio` group),
40	     `has_pixels` (bool: the clip has a `video` group and its source is not `adjustment`),
41	     `kind` (one of `media`, `still`, `image`, `text`, `shape`, `graphic`, `nest`, `adjustment`),
42	     `follows_clip` (bool: the clip starts at or before the end of the previous clip on its
43	     track) and `has_transition` (bool: its `transition_in` is not null). `{}` is any clip.
44	  4. *Step keys*, all optional: `reveal`, `spotlight`, `wait`, `show_me`, `optional`
45	     (`true`: Skip is offered, and finishing does not require the step).
46	  5. *`reveal`* is `{"tab": clip|media|document|assistant, "sub_tab"?: <a ClipSubTab raw
47	     value>, "section"?: <id>}`; `sub_tab` only with `tab` `clip`; a `section` must be in the
48	     app's target table and its home there must equal the step's `tab` and `sub_tab`.
49	  6. *`spotlight`* is one string: a fixed name of the app's target table, `section:<id>`
50	     (the id in the table), `clip:$selection` or `clip:$created`. The table is
51	     `app/Sources/TutorialTargets.swift`: the fixed names (`timeline.clips`, `ruler`,
52	     `canvas`, `toolbar.play`, `toolbar.timecode`, `toolbar.export`,
53	     `timeline.bar.{split,trim_start,trim_end,ripple_delete,add_marker,duplicate,add_text,
54	     add_shape}`, `inspector.tab.<the tab's title, lowercased>` and
55	     `inspector.sub_tab.<the sub-tab's raw value>` for every case, and
56	     `sheet.export.{format,size,frame_rate,quality,loudness,range,export,add_to_queue,
57	     cancel}`), and every inspector section id the app has, with its home tab and sub-tab.
58	     The checker also fails when the table's section ids and the `id: "<x>", title:`
59	     literals in `app/Sources` differ either way.
60	  7. *`wait`* holds at least one condition, and every one must hold: `selection` `{min?
61	     (an int ≥ 0, default 1), max? (an int ≥ min), …the filter's keys}` (every selected clip
62	     matches); `changed`, a path or a list of paths (a dotted clip-JSON path, met when any
63	     clip selected at the step's start differs there from its value at the start; the path
64	     must resolve in the checker's fixture clips); `clips` `{added: (an int ≥ 1), kind?}`;
65	     `playhead` `{inside: "$selection"|"$created"}`; `range`, exactly one of `{set: true}`
66	     and `{changed: "start"|"end"}`; `sheet` `"export"`; `export_started` `true` (the
67	     sheet's Export…, Add to Queue, or the `export` tool); `playing` `true`. A step with no
68	     `wait` shows Next.
69	  8. *`show_me`* is `{"tool": <name>, "args"?: {…}}`, `{"menu": "<A ▸ B[ ▸ C]>"}`, or a
70	     non-empty list of those, run in order. A tool is in the catalog and not a dev tool;
71	     every key of its `args` is in its `inputSchema.properties`; a literal string where the
72	     property has an `enum` is a member of it; for `set_video`, `set_audio`, `set_text` and
73	     `set_shape`, every leaf of `args.patch`, as `<group>.<path>`, resolves in the fixture
74	     clips. A menu is an item path of the built menu bar whose leaf's selector is a key of
75	     `tools/proof/capture_spike/inventory.json`'s `selectors`.
76	  9. *Variables*, inside `show_me` args only, at any depth: `"$selection"`, the clip ids at
77	     the step's start; `"$created"`, the ids added by the latest earlier step, or earlier
78	     call of this Show Me, that added any; `"$playhead"`, a tick; `{"$pick": <filter>}`, the
79	     id of the first matching clip in time order (ties: the front track first);
80	     `{"$first": "$selection"|"$created"}`, the earliest of those ids; `{"$time": {"of":
81	     <ref>, "at": start|middle|end}}`, a tick on the ref's span; `{"$track": "front"}`, the
82	     front track's id, resolved per call (so after an earlier `add_track` call of the same
83	     list it is that new, empty track). A `<ref>` is `"$selection"`, `"$created"`, a `$pick`
84	     or a `$first`. Any other `$`-string or `$`-key is refused.
85	  10. *Menu paths in a sentence.* `▸` appears only inside a bold span `**A ▸ B[ ▸ C]**`,
86	      which is a leaf or submenu path of the built menu bar whose leaf's selector is in
87	      `inventory.json`; the titles are spelled exactly (`Export…` with U+2026).
88	
89	  The checker reads the app's facts from a probe compiled over `app/Sources`

# Spec §11 — decisions: Tutorials (road map "tutorials")

Part of spec §11, *Decisions made — do not re-litigate*. The index of every decision is
[`README.md`](README.md).

The road map that makes these is in progress: `designs/tutorials.md` (TU0–TU4), whose
"Record" section holds each phase's record. TU-1..TU-6 were recorded in TU0, before any code;
TU-2's vocabulary was settled in TU1 and is normative here, not in the road map. TU-7 was recorded in
TU1b, before its code. The owner's
answers of 2026-10-31 (the road map's §10) are marked "owner": the five model tutorials kept,
a bundled practice project built now, and the word "Tutorials".

- **TU-1 — One source: a tutorial is an ordinary numbered list in its feature's guide page,
  and its machine half is an HTML comment at the end of each item.** The sentence a reader
  follows on GitHub is the sentence the app shows, word for word, because both are the same
  lines; no second set of docs is started, and a tutorial cannot drift from its page. A
  heading `### Tutorial: <title>` opens one, and a `<!-- tutorial {json} -->` line under it
  names it. Every Markdown viewer hides the comments, so a reader sees plain steps.
  `tools/tutorials/tutorial_extract.py` reads every page of `docs/guide/` and the app build's
  "Write Tutorials" step writes its output into the bundle as `Tutorials.json`:
  `{"format": 1, "pages": [{"page", "title" (the page's H1), "tutorials": [{"id", "title",
  "anchor" (the heading's GitHub slug), "needs" (default `{}`), "steps": [{"text", …the
  step's machine-half keys verbatim}]}]}]}`, pages sorted by file name, only pages that hold
  a tutorial, `json.dumps(indent=1, ensure_ascii=False)`. The extractor refuses a page whose
  tutorial breaks the structure of TU-2 (1), naming the page and the line, and the build
  fails. Risk accepted: a tutorial's words are the guide's register, written for a reader of
  the page, and the coach panel shows them as they are.
- **TU-2 — The step vocabulary is closed, and `tools/proof/tutorial_check.py` in `make test`
  refuses anything outside it, naming the page, the tutorial and the step.** The vocabulary:
  1. *Structure.* A heading `### Tutorial: <title>`; its next non-blank line starts
     `<!-- tutorial {json} -->`; then the first ordered list, numbered 1..n; an item's
     continuation lines are indented at least 3 spaces; an item may end with
     `<!-- step {json} -->` (the JSON may span lines), and nothing follows `-->` in the
     item; no `<!-- tutorial` or `<!-- step` appears anywhere else in the page. The step's
     sentence is the item's text less the comment, its lines joined by one space; it is
     never empty, and its Markdown is kept.
  2. *Tutorial keys.* `id`, required, matching `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*(\.[a-z][a-z0-9_]*)+$` and
     unique across the guide; `needs`, optional, `{"clip": <filter>}`.
  3. *Clip filter.* Optional `has_sound` (bool: the clip has an `audio` group),
     `has_pixels` (bool: the clip has a `video` group and its source is not `adjustment`),
     `kind` (one of `media`, `still`, `image`, `text`, `shape`, `graphic`, `nest`, `adjustment`),
     `follows_clip` (bool: the clip starts at or before the end of the previous clip on its
     track) and `has_transition` (bool: its `transition_in` is not null). `{}` is any clip.
  4. *Step keys*, all optional: `reveal`, `spotlight`, `wait`, `show_me`, `optional`
     (`true`: Skip is offered, and finishing does not require the step).
  5. *`reveal`* is `{"tab": clip|media|document|assistant, "sub_tab"?: <a ClipSubTab raw
     value>, "section"?: <id>}`; `sub_tab` only with `tab` `clip`; a `section` must be in the
     app's target table and its home there must equal the step's `tab` and `sub_tab`.
  6. *`spotlight`* is one string: a fixed name of the app's target table, `section:<id>`
     (the id in the table), `clip:$selection` or `clip:$created`. The table is
     `app/Sources/TutorialTargets.swift`: the fixed names (`timeline.clips`, `ruler`,
     `canvas`, `toolbar.play`, `toolbar.timecode`, `toolbar.export`,
     `timeline.bar.{split,trim_start,trim_end,ripple_delete,add_marker,duplicate,add_text,
     add_shape}`, `inspector.tab.<the tab's title, lowercased>` and
     `inspector.sub_tab.<the sub-tab's raw value>` for every case, and
     `sheet.export.{format,size,frame_rate,quality,loudness,range,export,add_to_queue,
     cancel}`), and every inspector section id the app has, with its home tab and sub-tab.
     The checker also fails when the table's section ids and the `id: "<x>", title:`
     literals in `app/Sources` differ either way.
  7. *`wait`* holds at least one condition, and every one must hold: `selection` `{min?
     (an int ≥ 0, default 1), max? (an int ≥ min), …the filter's keys}` (every selected clip
     matches); `changed`, a path or a list of paths (a dotted clip-JSON path, met when any
     clip selected at the step's start differs there from its value at the start; the path
     must resolve in the checker's fixture clips); `clips` `{added: (an int ≥ 1), kind?}`;
     `playhead` `{inside: "$selection"|"$created"}`; `range`, exactly one of `{set: true}`
     and `{changed: "start"|"end"}`; `sheet` `"export"`; `export_started` `true` (the
     sheet's Export…, Add to Queue, or the `export` tool); `playing` `true`. A step with no
     `wait` shows Next.
  8. *`show_me`* is `{"tool": <name>, "args"?: {…}}`, `{"menu": "<A ▸ B[ ▸ C]>"}`, or a
     non-empty list of those, run in order. A tool is in the catalog and not a dev tool;
     every key of its `args` is in its `inputSchema.properties`; a literal string where the
     property has an `enum` is a member of it; for `set_video`, `set_audio`, `set_text` and
     `set_shape`, every leaf of `args.patch`, as `<group>.<path>`, resolves in the fixture
     clips. A menu is an item path of the built menu bar whose leaf's selector is a key of
     `tools/proof/capture_spike/inventory.json`'s `selectors`.
  9. *Variables*, inside `show_me` args only, at any depth: `"$selection"`, the clip ids at
     the step's start; `"$created"`, the ids added by the latest earlier step, or earlier
     call of this Show Me, that added any; `"$playhead"`, a tick; `{"$pick": <filter>}`, the
     id of the first matching clip in time order (ties: the front track first);
     `{"$first": "$selection"|"$created"}`, the earliest of those ids; `{"$time": {"of":
     <ref>, "at": start|middle|end}}`, a tick on the ref's span; `{"$track": "front"}`, the
     front track's id, resolved per call (so after an earlier `add_track` call of the same
     list it is that new, empty track). A `<ref>` is `"$selection"`, `"$created"`, a `$pick`
     or a `$first`. Any other `$`-string or `$`-key is refused.
  10. *Menu paths in a sentence.* `▸` appears only inside a bold span `**A ▸ B[ ▸ C]**`,
      which is a leaf or submenu path of the built menu bar whose leaf's selector is in
      `inventory.json`; the titles are spelled exactly (`Export…` with U+2026).

  The checker reads the app's facts from a probe compiled over `app/Sources`
  (`tools/proof/tutorial_probe.swift`): the prepared catalog, the dev tools' names, the
  target table, the built menu bar and a fixture project's clips as the core writes them. A
  probe that does not build is a scored failure. TU1 settled the list beyond the road map's
  first draft: `$playhead`, `$first`, `$time`, `$track`, a list and a menu form of Show Me,
  `export_started` in place of `queued`, `range`'s `changed`, and the filter's
  `follows_clip` and `has_transition`. Risk accepted: a closed list means a new kind of step
  is a new entry here and a checker change before any tutorial can use it.
- **TU-3 — Show Me does the step the way the app already does it, and is an ordinary edit.**
  The tool form, and each tool entry of a list, runs through `AgentServer.execute`, the path
  the Assistant's calls take, through the argument gate; each edit it makes is an ordinary
  undo step. The menu form performs the built menu bar's own item: validated as a click
  validates it, its own action, the path a click takes, and no dev tool
  (`perform_menu_item` is not in Distribution). A list runs its entries in order. Exiting a
  tutorial undoes nothing. It adds no op and no new way to edit. Risk accepted: a Show Me
  edit is in the person's undo history like their own.
- **TU-4 — The coach panel is a small non-activating floating panel beside the editor
  window, and the spotlight a borderless, click-through child window over it.** The panel is
  the recorder panel's kind: it never takes key focus, so typing into an inspector field
  still goes to the field; it shows the title, "Step n of m", the sentence and Back, Show
  Me, Skip (on an optional step) and Exit. The spotlight is a window, so its ring sits above
  the Metal and `AVPlayerLayer` layers, and it follows the target when the layout moves.
- **TU-5 — A tutorial's `needs` are checked against the open project before step 1, and
  when they are not met the panel says what is missing and offers the practice project.**
  It does not start until they are met. The offer names the other way too (open a movie of
  your own). A `needs` is a clip filter (TU-2 (3)), so what a tutorial needs is written in
  the same words a wait uses.
- **TU-6 — The practice project is bundled with the app, its media made by a script checked
  in beside it, and it is opened as an untitled copy so the bundled one is never written
  (owner, 2026-10-31: build it now).** It holds at least two clips with sound that meet on
  one track, room above them for a title, and enough length to set an in/out range and
  export it, so every model tutorial's `needs` are met in it, and it is kept so as the set
  grows. Its media carries no third-party footage or music, its provenance is written down in

  videos will film.
- **TU-7 — The practice project is a generated `.framejob` package in the bundle, opened as an

# app/CLAUDE.md — Swift app rules

Applies to everything under `app/`. Build/verification commands and the FFI
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is
`designs/spec/` (§3–4 the UI, §7.4–7.8 the platform side; its `README.md` is
the index). The
long form of each entry below — why each file is the shape it is, and the
traps its history turned up — is `designs/adr/app-file-history.md` (the
full history, every size toll and measurement, is archived; see its
"Original" line); this file is what governs a file now. Files
are listed by family; a file with a header comment of its own carries its
detail there.

## File map

**The core's edge.**
- `ReelCore.swift` — the **only** home for `rc_*` calls: `ReelProject`
  (handle + lazily decoded `ProjectSnapshot`; `json`, `snapshot` and
  `planJSON` are memoised PER HANDLE, so keep handles rather than minting
  them; so is `sourceMap(_:)`, `rc_project_source_map` decoded and checked
  once per handle and clip, SR-20), timecode, snapping (export presets/sizes/settings are
  `ExportValues.swift`'s, a pure move, HDR H-1), `ReelSpeed.limits` (the
  core's speed range and audio ceiling, typed as `SpeedLimits` in
  `CoreValues.swift` — no Swift file types a speed bound), `ReelColor` (`rc_normalise_color`, G-25), `ReelGraphicPackage` (`rc_graphic_package_write`, G-46; `read`, `rc_graphic_package_read`, G-47), `GraphicLibrary.usage()` (`rc_graphic_library_usage`) and
  `ReelContainer` (`rc_container_*`, a WebM/Matroska file's index,
  #216-R) and `ReelWebM` (`rc_webm_*`, the `av1_webm` writer, spec §11 CX-15) and `ReelHDR10` (`rc_hdr10_peak`, spec §11 HD-6; `av1Peak`,
  `rc_hdr10_av1_peak`, HD-18; `stillPeak`, `rc_hdr10_still_peak`, HD-20), and `GraphicLibrary.imageCache(limit:)`
  (`rc_graphic_image_cache`, G-39); `ReelCoreError`, `Fps.ffiPair` and `ReelTime`'s
  seconds conversions are `CoreValues.swift`'s (G6 phase 5's toll T2 and speed ramps SR4-0,
  pure moves); the typed patches are `TypedPatches.swift`'s (`VideoPatch`,
  `AudioPatch`, `ClipPatch`, the `ActionPatch` extension; a pure move, B73),
  `TextPatch` (with `case`, `words` and `word_style`) is `TextPatch.swift`'s,
  moved out so it could grow, and `ShapePatch` `ShapePatch.swift`'s (a pure
  move, the toll for `ReelColor`). `VideoPatch.color` is a sparse `ColorPatch`
  (`GradeProps.swift`, which holds `ColorAdjust` (moved out of
  `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, grading-2 G2-0) with its neutrality helpers, and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(tone:)`, and the wheels' `ColorWheel`, `ColorWheels`,
  `ColorWheelPatch`, `ColorWheelsPatch`, `ColorWheelKind` and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(wheels:)` (GR-11)); `VideoPatch.curves` is
  `CurveProps.swift`'s `ColorCurvesPatch`, beside `CurvePoint`,
  `CurveDomain`, `CurveChannel`, `CurveBlend` (a channel blended inside an
  action, spec §11 GR-34; `ColorCurves.blends`, never encoded), `ColorCurves` and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(curves:)` (GR-12, the hue curves GR-32; a
  pure move out of `GradeProps.swift`, grading-4 T4-0); `VideoPatch.qualifier` is
  `QualifierProps.swift`'s `ColorQualifierPatch`, beside `ColorQualifier` (its
  `blur`, `blursSelection` and `selectionSigma`, GR-35), `QualifierUniforms`
  (`blurred`, set only by `drawAdjustment`) and the pick's `QualifierSample`
  (GR-13), so a row writes
  only its own key to every selected clip. `word_style` has ONE
  app-side writer, `CaptionLayout.place` (W-10). `ReelAgentSocket` (road map
  14's MC2) wraps `rc_agent_socket_start` / `_release`: `start` throws the
  core's sentence, `release` is the quit's unlink-if-still-ours with no join.
  The `dictionary` extensions on the property types are
  `OpDictionaries.swift`'s (below).
  The graphics engine's wrappers are here too: `GraphicLibrary` (`addFont`,
  `addAsset`, `rasterize`, `families()`; frozen by its first compile,
  rasterize or `families()`) and
  `GraphicModule` (`compile`, `describeJSON`, `svg`; it holds its library
  strongly); their values `GraphicDiagnostic` (with `.error`, `.noModule`
  and `.of(_:)`, the one spelling of a diagnostic made from a message, a
  missing module or a thrown error), `GraphicFailure` (what a
  `diag_out` failure throws; `err_out` stays `ReelCoreError`) and
  `GraphicRaster` are `CoreValues.swift`'s, with `GraphicUsage`, the byte
  bridges `withByteBuffer` and `withMutableByteBuffer` (G-46's toll; never
  `UnsafeMutablePointer(mutating:)`), `SpeedLimits` (a pure move,
  clean-up batch 2), `ReelCoreError` and `Fps.ffiPair` (G6 phase 5's toll), and
  `CoreJSON` (`value`, `snapTicks`: `clipState`'s and `snapCandidates`' JSON
  halves, clean-up round 3's toll; `array`, `overrides`, C1's tolls; `ExportSize.list`,
  `ExportSettings.decoded`, `ReelAV1.Config.decoded`, `withNonNullBytes`, codec-export C5's
  toll), and C1's
  fix-pass moves: `ReelAV1.Config` / `.Color` (an extension of `ReelCore.swift`'s
  `ReelAV1`, whose `rc_av1_*` calls stay there), `GraphicDiagnostic.list(json:)`,
  `GraphicFailure.checkSides`, `SpeedLimits.decoded` and the free `withBytes`.
  `MediaDescriptor`, `MediaOriginal`, `mediaURL(for:)`, `originalURL(for:)`,
  `revealURL(for:)` (the original, else the copy), `isTrashed` and
  `bookmarkString(for:)` are `MediaDescriptor.swift`'s: a `media[]` element
  minus its id, and the media-file resolvers; they call no `rc_*`.
  It is also where the op table is read BACK: `ReelOp.coreNames()` over
  `rc_op_names`, and `ReelOp.coreSchemas()` over `rc_op_schemas` — every
  op's ARGUMENTS as JSON Schema, keyed by op name, which
  `AgentCatalog.opTool` prints for all sixty-two op tools.
  `deinit` frees the Rust allocation. It also holds **the one read of
  `rc_project_apply`'s TWO message channels**, in the header's own order — a
  sentence is a refusal, an error message is invalid input, neither written
  is an identity — answered as the `ReelEdit` below.
- `OpDictionaries.swift` — the `dictionary` extensions on the §5.2
  property types (`CropInsets` … `Gradient`), the model's own key names; a
  pure move out of `ReelCore.swift` (#190, issue batch B52b; road map 14's
  MC2 made the same move as `PropsDictionaries.swift`, and the merge kept
  main's file). With
  `ReelCore.swift` and `ReelOps.swift`, the only files that write an op
  argument. `putNullable` is the one writer of a three-state (`T??`)
  patch key: absent, an explicit null, or the value.
- `ReelOps.swift` — `OpArgs`, `ReelOp` and one typed factory per row of
  `core/src/edit.rs`'s op table, plus a RAW factory beside the typed one at
  each door that takes a CALLER's own object — ELEVEN of them (`setVideoRaw`,
  `setAudioRaw`, `setTextRaw`, `setShapeRaw`, `setClipRaw`,
  `setActionEndRaw`, `addTextClipRaw`, `addShapeClipRaw`, `setCanvasRaw`,
  `addBackgroundRaw`, `addZoomActionRaw`), which takes the
  caller's own object as `Any` — never `[String: Any]`, so a non-object is
  refused by the CORE in the words that name the group — and forwards it;
  there is no untyped op-JSON call site anywhere else. Where only ONE
  argument is the caller's (a colour, a region, a new clip's patch) the typed
  factory DELEGATES to the raw one, mapping its optional explicitly, because
  an `Optional<T>.none` widened to `Any?` is a non-nil `Any` wrapping a nil.
  The typed `setActionEnd` LIFTS every top-level null out of its patch into
  `off` (spec §11 CI-14: a typed `.some(nil)` is a switch turned OFF, kept
  at the end); `setActionEndRaw`'s nulls stay removals, which is what
  `clearOps` and every agent call send, and it writes `off` only when non-empty and `schema` only when non-nil
  (the agent door fills it for a graphic end from the module's current
  revision, spec §11 G-34).
  `addZoomActionRaw`'s region is `Any` and not `Any?`: an absent key and an
  explicit null are opposite intentions there, and only the tool can tell
  them apart.
  `scope` is a member folded into `json`; `documentLevelNames` MIRRORS
  `scope.rs`'s `refused_inside` (eight names) so one edit can mix a
  document-level op with scoped ones. A table, with
  `edit.rs`'s size exemption.
- `ReelOpSchema.swift` — what an op TAKES, mirroring what
  `core/src/op_schema.rs` publishes: the `properties` and `required` of one
  op's arguments, which are the two things `AgentServer.tool` takes, and
  `table(from:)`, which reads `rc_op_schemas`' JSON into them (SR4-0's pure
  move out of `ReelCore.swift`, whose `coreSchemas()` keeps the call). Here

**Frozen files.** `EditorViewController.swift`, `TimelineView.swift`,
`PreviewCanvasView.swift`, `AgentServer.swift` are **frozen at current
size**: anything adding more than ~50 lines goes in an extension file
(`EditorViewController+<Feature>.swift`, `TimelineView+<Feature>.swift`,
`AgentServer+<Feature>.swift`) or a new `…SheetController`, and the frozen
file keeps only the wiring — a stored property, a closure assignment, a
validator arm, a draw call. The pieces extension files build on are therefore
internal, not private. Pitfalls: a selector declared `@objc` on an extension
needs NO forward in the frozen file (a second declaration is an error); a
command whose body sits at the foot of a non-extension feature file carries
its validator arm there too, or the item falls through to the closing
`return true`; `handleEditorCharacter`'s bare-key `switch` matches in SOURCE
order, so a bare `case "x"` goes BELOW any modified `case "x" where …`; and
`handleEditorKey` refuses while a sheet is attached, because a sheet is
window-modal and the preview panel's forwarded keys would otherwise reach
the key map behind it.

**Playback and rendering.**
- `Playback.swift` (+`Meter`, +`PreviewQuality`, +`Step`, +`Scope`, +`Prefetch`) — one
  `AVPlayer` over the plan's composition; the transport, JKL, the rate KVO; `+Meter` is the level meter, moved out under
  the size rule; `+Scope` also holds `seekFinished()` and `report(_:)`
  (hdr H-3's pure move). `recompose()` re-colours the player's copy of the
  composition without a rebuild (`previewComposition(…, sdrVersion:)`, the
  way Preview Quality does): View ▸ Show SDR Version, spec §11 HD-14. **Only a seek someone ASKED for reports a time**:
  `seek(to:)` is that door, and Playback's own RESTORES — the rebuild's item
  swap and re-seek, the paused refresh's round trip — go through `startSeek`
  silently and report once, only if they come to rest off the last reported
  tick; a scope change seeks through `seekAfterRebuild(to:)`: its time is the
  NEW container's, so the outgoing item is neither sought nor heard and the
  rebuild in flight lands there, heard once (#130, `scope_playhead_probe.py`);
  an asked seek that arrives while a restore is seeking is heard once, when it
  lands; `update`'s same-plan and empty-plan arms discard a rebuild in flight;
  a held scope change whose rebuild fails, or whose new plan is empty, drops
  the item rather than leave the outgoing one, keeps its time and is heard
  once (`endHoldWithoutItem` in `+Scope`, #185; the seek flags are internal
  for `+Scope` alone); `rebuildHop` is the probe's seam, nil in the app, and
  its block takes an error it delivers as the build's failure; `report(_:)` is the one
  caller of `onTimeChanged`. While paused, an observer callback is heard only
  for the tick the player is at or seeking to, and only when it differs from
  the last report — a late callback for a superseded seek or a swapped-out
  item is dropped (#204, #209; `playhead_echo_probe.py` twice·1, pause·1) —
  and every seek's landing reports its rest once when it differs. `+Step`
  also holds the main hop `onMain`. `+Prefetch` is the playing preview's
  graphics prefetch (spec §11 G-36, #127): `syncPrefetch(from:seeking:)`,
  called from the rate KVO, `startSeek` (with the seek's TARGET, never
  `currentTime`, which still reads the player there) and `update`'s
  same-plan arm while playing, and stopped in `invalidate` and `deinit`;
  `recipeKey` is internal for it. `syncPrefetch` first notes activity for
  Background render, and `startBackgroundRender` (G-38) starts a paused pass
  on the composition's grid (`prefetchGrid`), answering why not
  (`.busy` re-arms the clock, `.notNeeded` waits for the next activity). An echoed restore
  moved the playhead (0 and back on every rebuild), and the timeline reveals
  every moved playhead, so a clip drag yanked the view
  (`playhead_echo_probe.py`). **A paused refresh is a one-tick round trip**
  (`refreshPausedFrame`): a zero-tolerance seek to the current time is a
  NO-OP on macOS 26.5.1, so the refresh seeks one tick off and returns; parked
  at the end it rests on the last frame's final tick, because the end tick
  composes black. Do not put a same-time seek back. Preview Quality overrides
  `renderSize` on a copy of the builder's
  `BuiltComposition.videoConfiguration` here (`Playback.previewComposition`,
  static so `phase8_chrome.py` calls it), keeping the
  canvas's EXACT aspect (`m · (w/g, h/g)`, coarser when the divisor does not
  divide `g`, Full for a coprime canvas); `AVPlayerItem.videoComposition` is
  a COPY property, so the setter re-assigns. `makePreviewLayer` is the one
  door to a second `AVPlayerLayer`.
  The item is dropped only for an EMPTY timeline (`plan.duration <= 0`,
  where the transport beeps). Never gate it on the plan's track lists: a
  timeline of only graphics, text, shapes or images has no plan track and
  plays over the builder's placeholder (road map 10 §10.8,
  `media_less_playback_probe.py`).

  `withoutCredential` and then bounded at 64 Unicode scalars (`bounded`,

  the id still owed a delete.

- `MediaTranscript.swift` — `cache/transcripts/<id>.json` and its

  in + duration × speed`, landing at `start + (m − in) / speed`, clamped

- `Transcriber.swift` (+`Languages`, +`Extract`, +`Jobs`) ·
