# app/CLAUDE.md — Swift app rules

Applies to everything under `app/`. Build/verification commands and the FFI
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is
`designs/spec/` (§3–4 the UI, §7.4–7.8 the platform side; its `README.md` is
the index). The
long form of each entry below — why each file is the shape it is, and the
traps its history turned up — is `designs/adr/app-file-history.md` (the
full history, every size toll and measurement, is archived; see its
"Original" line); this file is what governs a file now. Files
are listed by family; a file with a header comment of its own carries its
detail there.

## File map

**The core's edge.**
- `ReelCore.swift` — the **only** home for `rc_*` calls: `ReelProject`
  (handle + lazily decoded `ProjectSnapshot`; `json`, `snapshot` and
  `planJSON` are memoised PER HANDLE, so keep handles rather than minting
  them; so is `sourceMap(_:)`, `rc_project_source_map` decoded and checked
  once per handle and clip, SR-20), timecode, snapping (export presets/sizes/settings are
  `ExportValues.swift`'s, a pure move, HDR H-1), `ReelSpeed.limits` (the
  core's speed range and audio ceiling, typed as `SpeedLimits` in
  `CoreValues.swift` — no Swift file types a speed bound), `ReelColor` (`rc_normalise_color`, G-25), `ReelGraphicPackage` (`rc_graphic_package_write`, G-46; `read`, `rc_graphic_package_read`, G-47), `GraphicLibrary.usage()` (`rc_graphic_library_usage`) and
  `ReelContainer` (`rc_container_*`, a WebM/Matroska file's index,
  #216-R) and `ReelWebM` (`rc_webm_*`, the `av1_webm` writer, spec §11 CX-15) and `ReelHDR10` (`rc_hdr10_peak`, spec §11 HD-6; `av1Peak`,
  `rc_hdr10_av1_peak`, HD-18; `stillPeak`, `rc_hdr10_still_peak`, HD-20), and `GraphicLibrary.imageCache(limit:)`
  (`rc_graphic_image_cache`, G-39); `ReelCoreError`, `Fps.ffiPair` and `ReelTime`'s
  seconds conversions are `CoreValues.swift`'s (G6 phase 5's toll T2 and speed ramps SR4-0,
  pure moves); the typed patches are `TypedPatches.swift`'s (`VideoPatch`,
  `AudioPatch`, `ClipPatch`, the `ActionPatch` extension; a pure move, B73),
  `TextPatch` (with `case`, `words` and `word_style`) is `TextPatch.swift`'s,
  moved out so it could grow, and `ShapePatch` `ShapePatch.swift`'s (a pure
  move, the toll for `ReelColor`). `VideoPatch.color` is a sparse `ColorPatch`
  (`GradeProps.swift`, which holds `ColorAdjust` (moved out of
  `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, grading-2 G2-0) with its neutrality helpers, and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(tone:)`, and the wheels' `ColorWheel`, `ColorWheels`,
  `ColorWheelPatch`, `ColorWheelsPatch`, `ColorWheelKind` and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(wheels:)` (GR-11)); `VideoPatch.curves` is
  `CurveProps.swift`'s `ColorCurvesPatch`, beside `CurvePoint`,
  `CurveDomain`, `CurveChannel`, `CurveBlend` (a channel blended inside an
  action, spec §11 GR-34; `ColorCurves.blends`, never encoded), `ColorCurves` and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(curves:)` (GR-12, the hue curves GR-32; a
  pure move out of `GradeProps.swift`, grading-4 T4-0); `VideoPatch.qualifier` is
  `QualifierProps.swift`'s `ColorQualifierPatch`, beside `ColorQualifier` (its
  `blur`, `blursSelection` and `selectionSigma`, GR-35), `QualifierUniforms`
  (`blurred`, set only by `drawAdjustment`) and the pick's `QualifierSample`
  (GR-13), so a row writes
  only its own key to every selected clip. `word_style` has ONE
  app-side writer, `CaptionLayout.place` (W-10). `ReelAgentSocket` (road map
  14's MC2) wraps `rc_agent_socket_start` / `_release`: `start` throws the
  core's sentence, `release` is the quit's unlink-if-still-ours with no join.
  The `dictionary` extensions on the property types are
  `OpDictionaries.swift`'s (below).
  The graphics engine's wrappers are here too: `GraphicLibrary` (`addFont`,
  `addAsset`, `rasterize`, `families()`; frozen by its first compile,
  rasterize or `families()`) and
  `GraphicModule` (`compile`, `describeJSON`, `svg`; it holds its library
  strongly); their values `GraphicDiagnostic` (with `.error`, `.noModule`
  and `.of(_:)`, the one spelling of a diagnostic made from a message, a
  missing module or a thrown error), `GraphicFailure` (what a
  `diag_out` failure throws; `err_out` stays `ReelCoreError`) and
  `GraphicRaster` are `CoreValues.swift`'s, with `GraphicUsage`, the byte
  bridges `withByteBuffer` and `withMutableByteBuffer` (G-46's toll; never
  `UnsafeMutablePointer(mutating:)`), `SpeedLimits` (a pure move,
  clean-up batch 2), `ReelCoreError` and `Fps.ffiPair` (G6 phase 5's toll), and
  `CoreJSON` (`value`, `snapTicks`: `clipState`'s and `snapCandidates`' JSON
  halves, clean-up round 3's toll; `array`, `overrides`, C1's tolls; `ExportSize.list`,
  `ExportSettings.decoded`, `ReelAV1.Config.decoded`, `withNonNullBytes`, codec-export C5's
  toll), and C1's
  fix-pass moves: `ReelAV1.Config` / `.Color` (an extension of `ReelCore.swift`'s
  `ReelAV1`, whose `rc_av1_*` calls stay there), `GraphicDiagnostic.list(json:)`,
  `GraphicFailure.checkSides`, `SpeedLimits.decoded` and the free `withBytes`.
  `MediaDescriptor`, `MediaOriginal`, `mediaURL(for:)`, `originalURL(for:)`,
  `revealURL(for:)` (the original, else the copy), `isTrashed` and
  `bookmarkString(for:)` are `MediaDescriptor.swift`'s: a `media[]` element
  minus its id, and the media-file resolvers; they call no `rc_*`.
  It is also where the op table is read BACK: `ReelOp.coreNames()` over
  `rc_op_names`, and `ReelOp.coreSchemas()` over `rc_op_schemas` — every
  op's ARGUMENTS as JSON Schema, keyed by op name, which
  `AgentCatalog.opTool` prints for all sixty-two op tools.
  `deinit` frees the Rust allocation. It also holds **the one read of
  `rc_project_apply`'s TWO message channels**, in the header's own order — a
  sentence is a refusal, an error message is invalid input, neither written
  is an identity — answered as the `ReelEdit` below.
- `OpDictionaries.swift` — the `dictionary` extensions on the §5.2
  property types (`CropInsets` … `Gradient`), the model's own key names; a
  pure move out of `ReelCore.swift` (#190, issue batch B52b; road map 14's
  MC2 made the same move as `PropsDictionaries.swift`, and the merge kept
  main's file). With
  `ReelCore.swift` and `ReelOps.swift`, the only files that write an op
  argument. `putNullable` is the one writer of a three-state (`T??`)
  patch key: absent, an explicit null, or the value.
- `ReelOps.swift` — `OpArgs`, `ReelOp` and one typed factory per row of
  `core/src/edit.rs`'s op table, plus a RAW factory beside the typed one at
  each door that takes a CALLER's own object — ELEVEN of them (`setVideoRaw`,
  `setAudioRaw`, `setTextRaw`, `setShapeRaw`, `setClipRaw`,
  `setActionEndRaw`, `addTextClipRaw`, `addShapeClipRaw`, `setCanvasRaw`,
  `addBackgroundRaw`, `addZoomActionRaw`), which takes the
  caller's own object as `Any` — never `[String: Any]`, so a non-object is
  refused by the CORE in the words that name the group — and forwards it;
  there is no untyped op-JSON call site anywhere else. Where only ONE
  argument is the caller's (a colour, a region, a new clip's patch) the typed
  factory DELEGATES to the raw one, mapping its optional explicitly, because
  an `Optional<T>.none` widened to `Any?` is a non-nil `Any` wrapping a nil.
  The typed `setActionEnd` LIFTS every top-level null out of its patch into
  `off` (spec §11 CI-14: a typed `.some(nil)` is a switch turned OFF, kept
  at the end); `setActionEndRaw`'s nulls stay removals, which is what
  `clearOps` and every agent call send, and it writes `off` only when non-empty and `schema` only when non-nil
  (the agent door fills it for a graphic end from the module's current
  revision, spec §11 G-34).
  `addZoomActionRaw`'s region is `Any` and not `Any?`: an absent key and an
  explicit null are opposite intentions there, and only the tool can tell
  them apart.
  `scope` is a member folded into `json`; `documentLevelNames` MIRRORS
  `scope.rs`'s `refused_inside` (eight names) so one edit can mix a
  document-level op with scoped ones. A table, with
  `edit.rs`'s size exemption.
- `ReelOpSchema.swift` — what an op TAKES, mirroring what
  `core/src/op_schema.rs` publishes: the `properties` and `required` of one
  op's arguments, which are the two things `AgentServer.tool` takes, and
  `table(from:)`, which reads `rc_op_schemas`' JSON into them (SR4-0's pure
  move out of `ReelCore.swift`, whose `coreSchemas()` keeps the call). Here
  rather than next door for `ReelEdit.swift`'s reason — it names no `rc_*`
  symbol — and `properties` stays `[String: Any]` because a Swift type per
  kind would be another spelling of the table.
- `ReelEdit.swift` — what an op ANSWERS, mirroring `core/src/outcome.rs`:
  `ReelEdit` (`.applied` / `.identity` / `.refused`), `ReelRefusal` (the op
  the core declined and the rule's own sentence, carried verbatim), and the
  fold that applies a LIST — which names no `rc_*` symbol, so it lives here
  and not next door. **Only `.applied` is an undo step**; the other two are
  both "the project did not change" and differ only in what a caller can
  SAY. `.project` is the spelling for a caller that treats a refusal as
  nothing happened (a probe, a live drag), and there is one on
  `ReelEdit?` too for the `try?` probes. In the fold **a refusal does not
  stop the list** — a later op still runs after one, exactly as after an
  identity — and the FIRST refusal is answered only when nothing applied.
- `ProjectSnapshot.swift` · `TextProps.swift` · `MotionProps.swift` ·
  `WordProps.swift` · `MediaSnapshot.swift` · `ActionSnapshot.swift` · `ShapeProps.swift` · `CompositionPlan.swift` · `GradeProps.swift` · `CurveProps.swift` — the `Codable`, READ-ONLY mirror
  of spec §5.2 every view draws from. READ-ONLY means never written back as
  is: the stored properties are `var`, so a writer edits a COPY
  (`var s = current(); s.blur = v`) rather than rebuilding one through the
  defaulted memberwise initialiser, which silently drops a field it does not
  spell out; `MotionProps.with(_:)` is motion's per-slot copy (#357). `CompositionPlan.swift` (a pure move out of
  `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, grading GR1) is the plan's Swift side (spec §7.2): `PlanSegment`,
  `PlanRamp`, `PlanTrack`, `PlanInstruction` and `CompositionPlan`; `PlanSpeedRamp.source` is
  its `map` as a `SourceMap`, checked once at decode and not a coding key (SR-20 (c)). `ShapeProps.swift` (a pure
  move out of `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, grading L3) holds the shape group: `StrokeProps`,
  `GradientStop`, `Gradient` and `ShapeProps`. `GradeProps.swift` holds `ColorAdjust` (a pure move out of `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, grading-2 G2-0) beside grading's other value types. `ActionSnapshot.swift` (a pure move out of
  `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, B87) holds `ActionPatch`, `ActionSnapshot` and `ActionGraphicPatch` — an
  end's `graphic.props` and `kinds`, whose `dictionary` sends `props` only. `MediaSnapshot` (a pure move out of
  `ProjectSnapshot.swift`) carries a copy's or an ffmpeg conversion's `original`, and its `name` is
  the one display-name spelling: the original's name when one is recorded. **Its enums decode LENIENTLY**
  — a misspelt kind becomes the first case, a `T??` field a clear — which is
  why a caller-authored object is never decoded through them (below). The
  one exception is `ClipSource`: an unknown `source.kind` THROWS, and
  `ReelProject.snapshot` then falls back to `.empty`, so the WHOLE project
  draws empty with no error. A new source kind in the core is therefore a
  `ClipSource` case in the same phase (road map 10's G2a added `graphic`): no
  agent handler reads a caller-authored OBJECT at all. A scalar enum
  argument is a different thing and several handlers still parse one by name
  (`enumArg` for `add_zoom_action`'s `fit` or an action's `curve`,
  `set_transition`'s `kind` by hand): the
  core refuses those too, and what this rule forbids is decoding a caller's
  object through a lenient type.
  `MotionProps.dictionary` always writes all three keys, `NSNull` for a nil
  slot, because a core patch of `motion` deep-merges — it is the
  APP's writer saying all three slots, not a replace rule, and it is the only
  edge that writes a whole motion. `MotionEdge` also supplies nonpersisted
  zero-duration activity and inactive display/menu titles (E2-27).
  `TextProps.swift` is the text group and `RecipeReveal` (with format version
  9's `textCase` / `words` / `wordStyle`, the recipe's `word` / `wordPop` and,
  since format version 12, `wordGlide` / `wordFill` / `wordDim`), a pure move
  out of `ProjectSnapshot.swift` because a stored property cannot be added
  from an extension. `RecipeReveal` reads and writes its OWN keys — siblings of
  `hash` and `text` in the `text` source — through `init(siblingsOf:)` and
  `encodeSiblings(to:)`, so a new recipe key costs `FrameRecipe.swift`
  nothing; a key spelled other than the snake-case converter spells it
  decodes silently to that key's default (the amount to 1, the rest to nil).
  `ProjectSnapshot+Graphic.swift` mirrors
  `model_graphic.rs`'s `GraphicProps` as `GraphicSnapshot` (`in` is
  `sourceIn`) and `GraphicPropValue` (string, number, bool; anything else
  `.null`), decoded into `ClipSnapshot.graphic`; `props` keys keep the
  module's own spelling (snake-case conversion does not reach a dictionary's
  keys). `WordProps.swift` mirrors `model_words.rs`
  (`TextCase`, `TextWord`, `WordMode`, `ActivePill`, `WordStyle`)
  — `WordStyle.dictionary` writes ALL eight keys (`active_fill` and `pause_dim` since format version 12; `ActivePill.dictionary` writes `glide`), `NSNull` for a nil slot,
  `MotionProps.dictionary`'s rule, because the core deep-merges
  `word_style` — and holds
  what the renderer and the inspector share: `laidContent` (`case` applied —
  every layout and string index is in ITS UTF-16 space, never `content`'s),
  `tokenCount`, `isUntimedPage`, `TextPatch.contentEdit` and

`PreviewCanvasView.swift`, `AgentServer.swift` are **frozen at current
size**: anything adding more than ~50 lines goes in an extension file
(`EditorViewController+<Feature>.swift`, `TimelineView+<Feature>.swift`,
`AgentServer+<Feature>.swift`) or a new `…SheetController`, and the frozen
file keeps only the wiring — a stored property, a closure assignment, a
validator arm, a draw call. The pieces extension files build on are therefore
internal, not private. Pitfalls: a selector declared `@objc` on an extension
needs NO forward in the frozen file (a second declaration is an error); a
command whose body sits at the foot of a non-extension feature file carries
its validator arm there too, or the item falls through to the closing
`return true`; `handleEditorCharacter`'s bare-key `switch` matches in SOURCE
order, so a bare `case "x"` goes BELOW any modified `case "x" where …`; and
`handleEditorKey` refuses while a sheet is attached, because a sheet is
window-modal and the preview panel's forwarded keys would otherwise reach
the key map behind it.

**Playback and rendering.**
- `Playback.swift` (+`Meter`, +`PreviewQuality`, +`Step`, +`Scope`, +`Prefetch`) — one
  `AVPlayer` over the plan's composition; the transport, JKL, the rate KVO; `+Meter` is the level meter, moved out under
  the size rule; `+Scope` also holds `seekFinished()` and `report(_:)`
  (hdr H-3's pure move). `recompose()` re-colours the player's copy of the
  composition without a rebuild (`previewComposition(…, sdrVersion:)`, the
  way Preview Quality does): View ▸ Show SDR Version, spec §11 HD-14. **Only a seek someone ASKED for reports a time**:
  `seek(to:)` is that door, and Playback's own RESTORES — the rebuild's item
  swap and re-seek, the paused refresh's round trip — go through `startSeek`
  silently and report once, only if they come to rest off the last reported
  tick; a scope change seeks through `seekAfterRebuild(to:)`: its time is the
  NEW container's, so the outgoing item is neither sought nor heard and the
  rebuild in flight lands there, heard once (#130, `scope_playhead_probe.py`);
  an asked seek that arrives while a restore is seeking is heard once, when it
  lands; `update`'s same-plan and empty-plan arms discard a rebuild in flight;
  a held scope change whose rebuild fails, or whose new plan is empty, drops
  the item rather than leave the outgoing one, keeps its time and is heard
  once (`endHoldWithoutItem` in `+Scope`, #185; the seek flags are internal
  for `+Scope` alone); `rebuildHop` is the probe's seam, nil in the app, and
  its block takes an error it delivers as the build's failure; `report(_:)` is the one
  caller of `onTimeChanged`. While paused, an observer callback is heard only
  for the tick the player is at or seeking to, and only when it differs from
  the last report — a late callback for a superseded seek or a swapped-out
  item is dropped (#204, #209; `playhead_echo_probe.py` twice·1, pause·1) —
  and every seek's landing reports its rest once when it differs. `+Step`
  also holds the main hop `onMain`. `+Prefetch` is the playing preview's
  graphics prefetch (spec §11 G-36, #127): `syncPrefetch(from:seeking:)`,
  called from the rate KVO, `startSeek` (with the seek's TARGET, never
  `currentTime`, which still reads the player there) and `update`'s
  same-plan arm while playing, and stopped in `invalidate` and `deinit`;
  `recipeKey` is internal for it. `syncPrefetch` first notes activity for
  Background render, and `startBackgroundRender` (G-38) starts a paused pass
  on the composition's grid (`prefetchGrid`), answering why not
  (`.busy` re-arms the clock, `.notNeeded` waits for the next activity). An echoed restore
  moved the playhead (0 and back on every rebuild), and the timeline reveals
  every moved playhead, so a clip drag yanked the view
  (`playhead_echo_probe.py`). **A paused refresh is a one-tick round trip**
  (`refreshPausedFrame`): a zero-tolerance seek to the current time is a
  NO-OP on macOS 26.5.1, so the refresh seeks one tick off and returns; parked
  at the end it rests on the last frame's final tick, because the end tick
  composes black. Do not put a same-time seek back. Preview Quality overrides
  `renderSize` on a copy of the builder's
  `BuiltComposition.videoConfiguration` here (`Playback.previewComposition`,
  static so `phase8_chrome.py` calls it), keeping the
  canvas's EXACT aspect (`m · (w/g, h/g)`, coarser when the divisor does not
  divide `g`, Full for a coprime canvas); `AVPlayerItem.videoComposition` is
  a COPY property, so the setter re-assigns. `makePreviewLayer` is the one
  door to a second `AVPlayerLayer`.
  The item is dropped only for an EMPTY timeline (`plan.duration <= 0`,
  where the transport beeps). Never gate it on the plan's track lists: a
  timeline of only graphics, text, shapes or images has no plan track and
  plays over the builder's placeholder (road map 10 §10.8,
  `media_less_playback_probe.py`).

1	# Spec §11 — decisions: Tutorials (road map "tutorials")
2	
3	Part of spec §11, *Decisions made — do not re-litigate*. The index of every decision is
4	[`README.md`](README.md).
5	
6	The road map that makes these is in progress: `designs/tutorials.md` (TU0–TU4), whose
7	"Record" section holds each phase's record. TU-1..TU-6 were recorded in TU0, before any code;
8	TU-2's vocabulary was settled in TU1 and is normative here, not in the road map. TU-7 was recorded in
9	TU1b, before its code. The owner's
10	answers of 2026-10-31 (the road map's §10) are marked "owner": the five model tutorials kept,
11	a bundled practice project built now, and the word "Tutorials".
12	
13	- **TU-1 — One source: a tutorial is an ordinary numbered list in its feature's guide page,
14	  and its machine half is an HTML comment at the end of each item.** The sentence a reader
15	  follows on GitHub is the sentence the app shows, word for word, because both are the same
16	  lines; no second set of docs is started, and a tutorial cannot drift from its page. A
17	  heading `### Tutorial: <title>` opens one, and a `<!-- tutorial {json} -->` line under it
18	  names it. Every Markdown viewer hides the comments, so a reader sees plain steps.
19	  `tools/tutorials/tutorial_extract.py` reads every page of `docs/guide/` and the app build's
20	  "Write Tutorials" step writes its output into the bundle as `Tutorials.json`:
21	  `{"format": 1, "pages": [{"page", "title" (the page's H1), "tutorials": [{"id", "title",
22	  "anchor" (the heading's GitHub slug), "needs" (default `{}`), "steps": [{"text", …the
23	  step's machine-half keys verbatim}]}]}]}`, pages sorted by file name, only pages that hold
24	  a tutorial, `json.dumps(indent=1, ensure_ascii=False)`. The extractor refuses a page whose
25	  tutorial breaks the structure of TU-2 (1), naming the page and the line, and the build
26	  fails. Risk accepted: a tutorial's words are the guide's register, written for a reader of
27	  the page, and the coach panel shows them as they are.
28	- **TU-2 — The step vocabulary is closed, and `tools/proof/tutorial_check.py` in `make test`
29	  refuses anything outside it, naming the page, the tutorial and the step.** The vocabulary:
30	  1. *Structure.* A heading `### Tutorial: <title>`; its next non-blank line starts
31	     `<!-- tutorial {json} -->`; then the first ordered list, numbered 1..n; an item's
32	     continuation lines are indented at least 3 spaces; an item may end with
33	     `<!-- step {json} -->` (the JSON may span lines), and nothing follows `-->` in the
34	     item; no `<!-- tutorial` or `<!-- step` appears anywhere else in the page. The step's
35	     sentence is the item's text less the comment, its lines joined by one space; it is
36	     never empty, and its Markdown is kept.
37	  2. *Tutorial keys.* `id`, required, matching `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*(\.[a-z][a-z0-9_]*)+$` and
38	     unique across the guide; `needs`, optional, `{"clip": <filter>}`.
39	  3. *Clip filter.* Optional `has_sound` (bool: the clip has an `audio` group),
40	     `has_pixels` (bool: the clip has a `video` group and its source is not `adjustment`),
41	     `kind` (one of `media`, `still`, `image`, `text`, `shape`, `graphic`, `nest`, `adjustment`),
42	     `follows_clip` (bool: the clip starts at or before the end of the previous clip on its
43	     track) and `has_transition` (bool: its `transition_in` is not null). `{}` is any clip.
44	  4. *Step keys*, all optional: `reveal`, `spotlight`, `wait`, `show_me`, `optional`
45	     (`true`: Skip is offered, and finishing does not require the step).
46	  5. *`reveal`* is `{"tab": clip|media|document|assistant, "sub_tab"?: <a ClipSubTab raw
47	     value>, "section"?: <id>}`; `sub_tab` only with `tab` `clip`; a `section` must be in the
48	     app's target table and its home there must equal the step's `tab` and `sub_tab`.
49	  6. *`spotlight`* is one string: a fixed name of the app's target table, `section:<id>`
50	     (the id in the table), `clip:$selection` or `clip:$created`. The table is
51	     `app/Sources/TutorialTargets.swift`: the fixed names (`timeline.clips`, `ruler`,
52	     `canvas`, `toolbar.play`, `toolbar.timecode`, `toolbar.export`,
53	     `timeline.bar.{split,trim_start,trim_end,ripple_delete,add_marker,duplicate,add_text,
54	     add_shape}`, `inspector.tab.<the tab's title, lowercased>` and
55	     `inspector.sub_tab.<the sub-tab's raw value>` for every case, and
56	     `sheet.export.{format,size,frame_rate,quality,loudness,range,export,add_to_queue,
57	     cancel}`), and every inspector section id the app has, with its home tab and sub-tab.
58	     The checker also fails when the table's section ids and the `id: "<x>", title:`
59	     literals in `app/Sources` differ either way.
60	  7. *`wait`* holds at least one condition, and every one must hold: `selection` `{min?
61	     (an int ≥ 0, default 1), max? (an int ≥ min), …the filter's keys}` (every selected clip
62	     matches); `changed`, a path or a list of paths (a dotted clip-JSON path, met when any
63	     clip selected at the step's start differs there from its value at the start; the path
64	     must resolve in the checker's fixture clips); `clips` `{added: (an int ≥ 1), kind?}`;
65	     `playhead` `{inside: "$selection"|"$created"}`; `range`, exactly one of `{set: true}`
66	     and `{changed: "start"|"end"}`; `sheet` `"export"`; `export_started` `true` (the
67	     sheet's Export…, Add to Queue, or the `export` tool); `playing` `true`. A step with no
68	     `wait` shows Next.
69	  8. *`show_me`* is `{"tool": <name>, "args"?: {…}}`, `{"menu": "<A ▸ B[ ▸ C]>"}`, or a
70	     non-empty list of those, run in order. A tool is in the catalog and not a dev tool;
71	     every key of its `args` is in its `inputSchema.properties`; a literal string where the
72	     property has an `enum` is a member of it; for `set_video`, `set_audio`, `set_text` and
73	     `set_shape`, every leaf of `args.patch`, as `<group>.<path>`, resolves in the fixture
74	     clips. A menu is an item path of the built menu bar whose leaf's selector is a key of
75	     `tools/proof/capture_spike/inventory.json`'s `selectors`.
76	  9. *Variables*, inside `show_me` args only, at any depth: `"$selection"`, the clip ids at
77	     the step's start; `"$created"`, the ids added by the latest earlier step, or earlier
78	     call of this Show Me, that added any; `"$playhead"`, a tick; `{"$pick": <filter>}`, the
79	     id of the first matching clip in time order (ties: the front track first);
80	     `{"$first": "$selection"|"$created"}`, the earliest of those ids; `{"$time": {"of":
81	     <ref>, "at": start|middle|end}}`, a tick on the ref's span; `{"$track": "front"}`, the
82	     front track's id, resolved per call (so after an earlier `add_track` call of the same
83	     list it is that new, empty track). A `<ref>` is `"$selection"`, `"$created"`, a `$pick`
84	     or a `$first`. Any other `$`-string or `$`-key is refused.
85	  10. *Menu paths in a sentence.* `▸` appears only inside a bold span `**A ▸ B[ ▸ C]**`,
86	      which is a leaf or submenu path of the built menu bar whose leaf's selector is in
87	      `inventory.json`; the titles are spelled exactly (`Export…` with U+2026).
88	
89	  The checker reads the app's facts from a probe compiled over `app/Sources`
90	  (`tools/proof/tutorial_probe.swift`): the prepared catalog, the dev tools' names, the
91	  target table, the built menu bar and a fixture project's clips as the core writes them. A
92	  probe that does not build is a scored failure. TU1 settled the list beyond the road map's
93	  first draft: `$playhead`, `$first`, `$time`, `$track`, a list and a menu form of Show Me,
94	  `export_started` in place of `queued`, `range`'s `changed`, and the filter's
95	  `follows_clip` and `has_transition`. Risk accepted: a closed list means a new kind of step
96	  is a new entry here and a checker change before any tutorial can use it.
97	- **TU-3 — Show Me does the step the way the app already does it, and is an ordinary edit.**
98	  The tool form, and each tool entry of a list, runs through `AgentServer.execute`, the path
99	  the Assistant's calls take, through the argument gate; each edit it makes is an ordinary
100	  undo step. The menu form performs the built menu bar's own item: validated as a click
101	  validates it, its own action, the path a click takes, and no dev tool
102	  (`perform_menu_item` is not in Distribution). A list runs its entries in order. Exiting a
103	  tutorial undoes nothing. It adds no op and no new way to edit. Risk accepted: a Show Me
104	  edit is in the person's undo history like their own.
105	- **TU-4 — The coach panel is a small non-activating floating panel beside the editor
106	  window, and the spotlight a borderless, click-through child window over it.** The panel is
107	  the recorder panel's kind: it never takes key focus, so typing into an inspector field
108	  still goes to the field; it shows the title, "Step n of m", the sentence and Back, Show
109	  Me, Skip (on an optional step) and Exit. The spotlight is a window, so its ring sits above
110	  the Metal and `AVPlayerLayer` layers, and it follows the target when the layout moves.
111	- **TU-5 — A tutorial's `needs` are checked against the open project before step 1, and
112	  when they are not met the panel says what is missing and offers the practice project.**
113	  It does not start until they are met. The offer names the other way too (open a movie of
114	  your own). A `needs` is a clip filter (TU-2 (3)), so what a tutorial needs is written in
115	  the same words a wait uses.
116	- **TU-6 — The practice project is bundled with the app, its media made by a script checked
117	  in beside it, and it is opened as an untitled copy so the bundled one is never written
118	  (owner, 2026-10-31: build it now).** It holds at least two clips with sound that meet on
119	  one track, room above them for a title, and enough length to set an in/out range and
120	  export it, so every model tutorial's `needs` are met in it, and it is kept so as the set
121	  grows. Its media carries no third-party footage or music, its provenance is written down in
122	  a `PROVENANCE.md`, it is a few megabytes at most, and the product still has no ffmpeg
123	  dependency. Help ▸ Tutorials ▸ Open Practice Project opens it, and a tutorial whose
124	  `needs` are unmet offers the same; it is what the tutorials' proof runs on and what the
125	  videos will film.
126	- **TU-7 — The practice project is a generated `.framejob` package in the bundle, opened as an
127	  untitled copy titled "Practice Project", and a saved copy owns its media.** The package is
128	  `Contents/Resources/Practice Project.framejob`: 1280×720 at 30 fps, three 8 s scenes (Dawn,
129	  Sea, Night), each placed as a 6 s clip with 1 s handles, back to back on Track 1 from 0 to

131	  Graphics and Core Text (no ffmpeg, in the product or the generator); the media paths in its
132	  `project.json` are placeholders that never resolve, re-anchored at open to the bundle's
133	  `media/` by the open path's own repair. `PracticeProject.open()` opens it untitled (no file),
134	  titled "Practice Project", clean until edited, so a save asks where; `new_project {practice:
135	  true}` is the agent's door, and Help ▸ Tutorials holds Open Practice Project last, so TU3's
136	  page submenus go above it. **A saved copy owns its media:** every write of a practice copy to
137	  a package — Save, Save As, an autosave in place, `save_project {path}`, `new_project
138	  {practice: true, path}` — puts the bundled files it uses into that package's `media/` and
139	  writes its `project.json` naming them there, inside the same atomic save; the open copy keeps
140	  playing the bundle's files until it is reopened; Consolidate relinks rather than copies a
141	  file already there; after the first save the window takes the file's name. **An open of a
142	  project inside the app never opens it in place:** Finder's doors open a practice copy, and
143	  `open_project` refuses, naming `new_project {practice: true}`. `tutorial_check.py` in `make
144	  test` checks every tutorial's `needs` against the package's clips, that its media resolve

  file and the history where they were and the journal put back as it was
  read (its bytes, or no file: `renameJournalBytes` / `putBackRenameJournal`
  in `GraphicStore+History.swift`), so a refused rename journals no pair; a
  crash between the three steps is G-28 (f)'s limit; neither rescans.
  `write(name:bytes:)` is `write(name:source:)` for bytes as they are, and
  `noModuleSentence(_:)` the one sentence for an absent module.
  `GraphicStore+History.swift` is the kept revisions and the rename journal
  (spec §11 G-27..G-29): `graphics/history/<name>/<%06d sequence>-<revision>.js`,
  the last `historyLimit` (10) per module, and `history/renames.json`, at
  most `renameJournalLimit` (32) pairs. `keepReplaced`, called by `pass` on
  the queue before it stores its scan, keeps the bytes a module's new text
  replaced and drops the new text's own revision, so history never holds the
  current text; nothing is kept at `start()` or for a removal the app did not
  make, and `start()` drops each module's current revision from its history.
  `history/` is created only inside an existing `graphics/` (G-14) with no
  `packageContentsDidChangeOnDisk()` call, and `moveHistory` leaves no
  `history/<from>/` behind — which is what makes 'no file, something kept'
  mean a DELETED module. `GraphicStore+Import.swift`'s `importAsset` files a name
  `asset(name)` cannot use under `GraphicAssetName.legalized`, a renamed
  copy taking `-2`, `-3`, … while `holdsAsset(named:)` (scan or disk) says
  the name is held, and answers `name`/`renamedFrom` (G-23 (c), (d)).

  under a name not yet taken, never replacing a file. **`drain()` is not
  re-entrant: never call `rescan()` from a `.graphicsDidChange` observer.**

**Frozen files.** `EditorViewController.swift`, `TimelineView.swift`,
`PreviewCanvasView.swift`, `AgentServer.swift` are **frozen at current
size**: anything adding more than ~50 lines goes in an extension file
(`EditorViewController+<Feature>.swift`, `TimelineView+<Feature>.swift`,
`AgentServer+<Feature>.swift`) or a new `…SheetController`, and the frozen
file keeps only the wiring — a stored property, a closure assignment, a
validator arm, a draw call. The pieces extension files build on are therefore
internal, not private. Pitfalls: a selector declared `@objc` on an extension
needs NO forward in the frozen file (a second declaration is an error); a
command whose body sits at the foot of a non-extension feature file carries
its validator arm there too, or the item falls through to the closing
`return true`; `handleEditorCharacter`'s bare-key `switch` matches in SOURCE
order, so a bare `case "x"` goes BELOW any modified `case "x" where …`; and
`handleEditorKey` refuses while a sheet is attached, because a sheet is
window-modal and the preview panel's forwarded keys would otherwise reach
the key map behind it.

**Playback and rendering.**
- `Playback.swift` (+`Meter`, +`PreviewQuality`, +`Step`, +`Scope`, +`Prefetch`) — one
  `AVPlayer` over the plan's composition; the transport, JKL, the rate KVO; `+Meter` is the level meter, moved out under
  the size rule; `+Scope` also holds `seekFinished()` and `report(_:)`
  (hdr H-3's pure move). `recompose()` re-colours the player's copy of the
  composition without a rebuild (`previewComposition(…, sdrVersion:)`, the
  way Preview Quality does): View ▸ Show SDR Version, spec §11 HD-14. **Only a seek someone ASKED for reports a time**:
  `seek(to:)` is that door, and Playback's own RESTORES — the rebuild's item
  swap and re-seek, the paused refresh's round trip — go through `startSeek`
  silently and report once, only if they come to rest off the last reported
  tick; a scope change seeks through `seekAfterRebuild(to:)`: its time is the
  NEW container's, so the outgoing item is neither sought nor heard and the
  rebuild in flight lands there, heard once (#130, `scope_playhead_probe.py`);
  an asked seek that arrives while a restore is seeking is heard once, when it
  lands; `update`'s same-plan and empty-plan arms discard a rebuild in flight;
  a held scope change whose rebuild fails, or whose new plan is empty, drops
  the item rather than leave the outgoing one, keeps its time and is heard
  once (`endHoldWithoutItem` in `+Scope`, #185; the seek flags are internal
  for `+Scope` alone); `rebuildHop` is the probe's seam, nil in the app, and
  its block takes an error it delivers as the build's failure; `report(_:)` is the one
  caller of `onTimeChanged`. While paused, an observer callback is heard only
  for the tick the player is at or seeking to, and only when it differs from
  the last report — a late callback for a superseded seek or a swapped-out
  item is dropped (#204, #209; `playhead_echo_probe.py` twice·1, pause·1) —
  and every seek's landing reports its rest once when it differs. `+Step`
  also holds the main hop `onMain`. `+Prefetch` is the playing preview's
  graphics prefetch (spec §11 G-36, #127): `syncPrefetch(from:seeking:)`,
  called from the rate KVO, `startSeek` (with the seek's TARGET, never
  `currentTime`, which still reads the player there) and `update`'s
  same-plan arm while playing, and stopped in `invalidate` and `deinit`;
  `recipeKey` is internal for it. `syncPrefetch` first notes activity for
  Background render, and `startBackgroundRender` (G-38) starts a paused pass
  on the composition's grid (`prefetchGrid`), answering why not
  (`.busy` re-arms the clock, `.notNeeded` waits for the next activity). An echoed restore
  moved the playhead (0 and back on every rebuild), and the timeline reveals
  every moved playhead, so a clip drag yanked the view
  (`playhead_echo_probe.py`). **A paused refresh is a one-tick round trip**
  (`refreshPausedFrame`): a zero-tolerance seek to the current time is a
  NO-OP on macOS 26.5.1, so the refresh seeks one tick off and returns; parked
  at the end it rests on the last frame's final tick, because the end tick
  composes black. Do not put a same-time seek back. Preview Quality overrides
  `renderSize` on a copy of the builder's
  `BuiltComposition.videoConfiguration` here (`Playback.previewComposition`,
  static so `phase8_chrome.py` calls it), keeping the
  canvas's EXACT aspect (`m · (w/g, h/g)`, coarser when the divisor does not
  divide `g`, Full for a coprime canvas); `AVPlayerItem.videoComposition` is
  a COPY property, so the setter re-assigns. `makePreviewLayer` is the one
  door to a second `AVPlayerLayer`.
  The item is dropped only for an EMPTY timeline (`plan.duration <= 0`,
  where the transport beeps). Never gate it on the plan's track lists: a
  timeline of only graphics, text, shapes or images has no plan track and
  plays over the builder's placeholder (road map 10 §10.8,
  `media_less_playback_probe.py`).

  `.vtt` from one all-text track, never guessed; a popup built from
  `NSMenuItem`s carrying `representedObject`, because `addItem(withTitle:)`
  REMOVES a same-titled row).
- `CloudTranscriber.swift` (+`Report`, +`Media`) — `TranscriptionEngine` (`apple` |
  `assemblyai`, persisted under `FrameJobCaptionEngine`) and the cloud engine
  over the SAME `Transcriber.Job` / `Outcome` / `CancelToken`. `run` is its
  serial queue and the main-thread completion; `transcribe` is the
  synchronous body — the janitor FIRST, the jobs grouped by MEDIA, each
  media classified cached / HELD / to upload, then each job's words cut out
  of its media's one transcript, through `captionWords` (fillers out,
  TR-1); the keyless admission asks `serves(.captions)`. `+Report` holds what the `Outcome` has no
  room for (`uploaded` with the transcript-write and marker-write results,
  `transcriptWritten` and `stampWritten`, `cached`,
  `janitorDeleted`, `janitorFailed`, `janitorDeferred`, `held`, and
  `refusedUndeleted` — a transcript refused after it was made whose DELETE
  failed, owed to the dashboard with no retry, R6-20) and owns the
  shared cleanup warning wording for the sheet and MCP result or failure.
  `billedSeconds` is the ONE sum of `audioSeconds` — each term floored at 0,
  saturating at `Int.max` — that the bill sentence and `audio_seconds` read;
  `cacheWarnings` is one sentence per uploaded media whose marker did not
  land, and promises nothing about the next run.
  A nil client admits only a nonempty, entirely
  current batch and skips janitor/network, retaining pending IDs as deferred.
  One media's failure is one media's problem (the catch first records a
  `Refusal` whose DELETE `failed` in `refusedUndeleted`, then reads its
  `ClientError`) and the run carries on, with exactly two exceptions: a CANCEL
  and a REFUSED KEY. `+Media` holds `retryDeletes` and `fetch` — the ten-hour
  refusal BEFORE the extract, the `defer` that removes the temporary audio on
  every exit, the server's model and language filtered through
  `withoutCredential` and then bounded at 64 Unicode scalars (`bounded`,
  `serverStringLimit`, #200), `audio_duration` floored at 0, words any of
  whose served strings — every key and value at any depth, scanned from the
  bytes (`TranscriptWord.servedStrings`, R6-23) — repeat the key refused
  (the transcript deleted) before any write, the cache file
  written before its marker, and the DELETE last with its answer recorded —
  its `remote_deleted` rewrite only over a first write that landed (#187).
  Spec §11's R6-11: a media in this run's
  `janitorFailed` is never fetched, since its cache file is the one record of
  the id still owed a delete.
- `CloudEstimate.swift` — what a cloud run would COST and why, PURE: a
  `Fate` per media (`upload(Reason)` / `cached` / `awaitingDelete(Reason)` /
  `unreadable`), `describe` (the sheet's summary line), `reasons` (one line
  per file that is not already transcribed, plus the DATED rate) and
  `money`, over `AssemblyAIRates`' two dated constants. Spec §11's R6-13: a
  media R6-11 will hold is its OWN clause and its line carries what it would
  cost if the delete clears. `facts(jobs:media:cacheDirectory:)` is the ONE
  member that opens a file, so a sheet can recompute the readout per
  keystroke. `canReuseWithoutCredential` is true only for nonempty all-cached
  rows and gates the keyless sheet. Its classification is deliberately NOT shared with
  `CloudTranscriber`'s — one says what a run WOULD do, the other what it DID
  — and a probe row compares them.
- `CloudProgress.swift` — the cloud run's one number and the words beside it,
  PURE: a share per media TO UPLOAD (cached and held media have none), the
  four phases at 0.25 / 0.65 / 0.95, the submit holding at the upload's end
  (0.65) with a line of its own, the wait advancing on the clock against q8's
  147× and holding, and the five detail lines, a count under a megabyte spelt
  `<1`. The run publishes
  `max(previous, computed)`.
- `AssemblyAITranscript.swift` — the wire VALUES, and
  `TranscriptOptions.keyterms`, the ONE spelling of the vocabulary's
  trim/de-duplicate/cap that the sheet's field and the tool's argument share:
  `TranscriptOptions`,
  `TranscriptRequest` (whose `encode` is the whole wire body — `language_code`
  absent for auto, `keyterms_prompt` absent when empty), `TranscriptWord`
  (with `servedStrings`, every string literal of a served `words` array
  decoded by a lexical scan, which `fetch` reads for the key),
  `TranscriptResponse` and `JSONValueRange`. `TranscriptStamp.swift` owns the
  cache marker: `TranscriptSourceStamp` projects `CacheStamp` to size,
  modification second, duration and audio presence, then pairs those with
  the provider and REQUEST (R6-15); old wide markers decode by projection.
  The request carries `disfluencies` (TR-2, always `true` on a new request;
  a marker or `requested` block without the key decodes it as false), and
  `serves(_:for:)` with `TranscriptUse` (`.captions`, `.fillers`) is the ONE
  currency comparison: every field but `disfluencies` must match, and
  `.fillers` also needs the marker's own `disfluencies` true.
  Nothing here speaks HTTP or touches disk. **Three encoders write every key
  with nil as `null`** through
  `encodeOrNull`, because `encodeIfPresent` would drop a key a cache file and
  its marker have to carry; `TranscriptResponse` reads `words` through a
  `try?` so the CLIENT's rule about a missing words array is the sentence a
  caller gets.
- `AssemblyAIClient.swift` (+`Session`, +`Submission`) — AssemblyAI's REST API as five
  SYNCHRONOUS calls over one `.ephemeral` `URLSession` with its own one-wide
  delegate queue (R6-7: no `async`). `willPerformHTTPRedirection` always
  answers nil, so a 3xx is `.redirected` and the credential reaches no other
  host; an upload retries once on a 5xx or a transport error and never on a
  4xx or after a cancel; `poll` sleeps in ≤ 0.1 s slices that read the token
  and EVERY throwing exit deletes the transcript first — `refusing`
  (`+Session`) answers a `Refusal` carrying that DELETE's answer
  (`deleted`/`failed`/`notSent`), which `CloudTranscriber.transcribe` unwraps
  before reading its `ClientError` (R6-20). A `completed` body
  whose `words` is absent, null or not an array is `.malformed`, never an
  empty transcript; `[]` is zero words. A `completed` body whose `id` is not
  the polled id is `.malformed` too (`requireEchoedID` in `+Session`, #71), so
  the id `fetch` stores and deletes is always the submitted one. `note` writes
  straight to fd 1 through `FileHandle.standardOutput`, never `print`, so a
  file-redirected log is complete (#116). `request` and `send` stay in the
  first file, with `withoutCredential(_:)` beside them: those three are the
  members that touch `credential`, and that helper keeps the three sentences
  the client RELAYS verbatim — a 402's, a 4xx's and a transcript's `error` —
  from carrying a key a server echoed back; `relayed` (`+Session`) then cuts
  each to 300 Unicode scalars (R6-23). `isSendableIdentifier`
  (`+Session`: `isPlainIdentifier` AND not `carriesCredential`) is the ONE id
  gate — `poll`, `delete`, a submit reply and a recovery-list row — so an id
  that carries the key is never sent or accepted. `delete` answers THREE
  states (`deleted`, `failed`, `notSent`): an id that is not sendable is never
  put on the wire. `delete(id:cancel:)` reads the run's token as a STOP and
  never attaches it: a DELETE is cut `deleteAfterStop` (2 s) of wall clock
  after the later of the Stop and its own start and answers `failed`, owed
  like any other (R6-19); `send`'s `stop`/`grace` and `+Session`'s
  `waitForReply` are that bound. `+Session` also holds `ClientError`'s two
  readings, `isRetriable` and `shortName`, moved out at the cap. `+Submission`
  owns the single paid submit and R6-14's
  bounded recovery: three newest-page looks for an exact uploaded URL, with
  no retry of the POST or requests by any unrelated id.
- `AssemblyAIConfiguration.swift` · `AssemblyAILanguages.swift` ·
  `SecretStore.swift` — WHERE the client speaks and WHAT it says it is.
  `AssemblyAIConfiguration` is the ONE reader of `-RCAssemblyAIEndpoint` and
  `-RCSecretFolder`, both out of the ARGUMENT domain only (its `argument` is
  the one argument-domain reader, which `AssistantConfiguration` and
  `DevAssistantLaunch` reuse), and the ONE line
  in the feature that names `AppSupport.directory` (spec §11's R6-9: with an
  endpoint set and no secret folder, `store()` answers an EMPTY `MemoryStore`
  so a proof never opens the person's key). `FileStore` has a `name`:
  `assemblyai-key` by default, `anthropic-key` for the assistant's key
  (AI-8, AI-13, whose `RC_ASSISTANT_BASE_URL` plays R6-9's endpoint). Non-`https` is accepted only for
  `127.0.0.1`, `localhost` and `::1`. `FileStore` creates its file with
  `O_CREAT|O_EXCL` at `0600` under a temporary name and `rename(2)`s it, in a
  directory `AppSupport.ensureDirectory` makes, `0700` at each level it makes
  — never `chmod`ed after; `MemoryStore` is
  the probe's. The language table is a DATED static list, not an authority:
  a code AssemblyAI refuses comes back as AssemblyAI's own sentence.
- `MediaTranscript.swift` — `cache/transcripts/<id>.json` and its
  `.complete.json` sidecar (`MediaImporter.transcriptsKind` is the post kind,
  and lives beside the other three in `MediaCacheFiles.swift`). The provider's
  `words` are stored VERBATIM as BYTES: `File.encoded()` splices `wordsJSON`
  in after a `.sortedKeys` header, `init(data:)` cuts it back out with
  `JSONValueRange`, and neither ever re-serialises — a `0.98` does not
  survive that. Both `File` inits throw on a `words` that is not an array, so
  `read` answers nil and `isCurrent` false rather than caching zero words;
  `isCurrent` asks `serves(_:for: .captions)`.
  THE MAPPING is here: a word is a clip's when `in ≤ start × 600 <
  in + duration × speed`, landing at `start + (m − in) / speed`, clamped
  through `Transcriber.placed` (R6-10). That `× 600` goes through
  `sourceTicks(milliseconds:)`, the one integer multiply on the caption
  path, clamped in `Int` to ±`Ticks.max / 600` first and deliberately NOT to
  `maxSourceTicks` (R6-10's extension). A RAMPED clip's job carries
  `Transcriber.Job.ramp` and lands a word at `clip.start + S⁻¹(m)` through
  its `SourceMap`, its window `[in, in + S(D))` (SR-20 (d)); the
  three-argument `Transcriber.jobs(for:in:urls:)` stays for the instruments
  and refuses a ramped clip.
  `undeleted(in:)` is the janitor's.
- `SpeechEngine.swift` — the on-device engine (`SpeechAnalyzer`,
  `SpeechTranscriber`, `AssetInventory`) and the ONE file under
  `app/Sources` that imports Speech or says `async` for it (spec §11 W-8).
  Every entry point is synchronous or a main-queue completion: `transcribe`
  refuses main by precondition and blocks its caller on a semaphore a
  `Task.detached` analysis signals, waited for in 0.1 s slices so a cancel
  answers at once, bounded at max(120, 4× the audio); the asks
  (`supportedLocales`, `installedLocales`, `isInstalled`) answer `[]` or nil
  past `askBound` (10 s); `download` is the Download row's alone and no tool
  calls it. **Never `Task {}` here** — a main-thread caller's actor would be
  inherited and the semaphore would deadlock. `Handle` is what
  `CancelToken` holds for a running analysis. Two host facts it is built on
  (road map 8 §10.6): `status(forModules:)` is `.installed` only for a
  RESERVED locale, so `isInstalled` reserves, reads and releases what it
  reserved; and `release(reservedLocale:)` matches the framework's own
  spelling (`fr_FR`, not `fr-FR`), so a release walks `reservedLocales` by
  BCP-47 tag. Every path that constructs a transcriber releases on every
  exit (a cap of 5). Reserve → status → release and every release run one
  at a time, in arrival order, through the `Gate` actor; `releaseNow` is the
  in-gate form, and an analysis or a download SIGNALS its caller before it
  queues its release, so a stalled gate cannot hold a finished run hostage.
- `Transcriber.swift` (+`Languages`, +`Extract`, +`Jobs`) ·
  `TranscribeSheetController.swift` (+`Cloud`: the AssemblyAI half — the
  Language popup's second population, `RunRequest` (the ONE function from
  the card's controls to what a run would receive), the estimate's readout,
  §5e's two hint texts, the notes and `beginCloud`; +`Commit`: the run's one
  exit, `cloudReportLines` and the menu command with its validator arm;

*Agents:* `split` takes `at` (the playhead when left out) and optional `clips`. Without `clips` it cuts every unlocked clip at that time.

### Tutorial: split a clip
<!-- tutorial {"id": "editing.split", "needs": {"clip": {}}} -->

1. Select a clip. <!-- step {"spotlight": "timeline.clips", "wait": {"selection": {}},
   "show_me": {"tool": "set_selection", "args": {"clips": [{"$pick": {}}]}}} -->
2. Put the playhead inside the clip: click the ruler above it, or drag along
   the ruler. <!-- step {"spotlight": "ruler", "wait": {"playhead": {"inside": "$selection"}},
   "show_me": {"tool": "set_playhead", "args": {"t": {"$time": {"of": "$selection", "at": "middle"}}}}} -->
3. Choose **Clip ▸ Split** (⌘T), or click the scissors in the timeline bar.

30	    /// for every format that has any, whether `loudness_lufs` was asked for
31	    /// or not.
32	    func exportProject(_ a: [String: Any]) throws -> String {
33	        // The clock `export_status`'s `elapsed` runs on, read before any check.
34	        let started = ProcessInfo.processInfo.systemUptime
35	        let presetID = try requiredString(a, "preset")
36	        let path = try requiredString(a, "path")
37	        let wholeProject = (try stringArg(a, "range") ?? "project").lowercased()
38	        guard ["project", "in_out"].contains(wholeProject) else {
39	            throw ToolError(
40	                message: "range must be \"project\" (the whole timeline) or \"in_out\" "
41	                    + "(the in/out range set_range set), not \"\(wholeProject)\".")
42	        }
43	        // The export sheet's burn-in checkbox — and read HERE rather than
44	        // into `overrides` below, which is the whole of the decision. A
45	        // recipe option changes the PICTURE, so it travels with the
46	        // description of the picture: `export_overrides.rs` ignores a key it
47	        // does not know, on purpose, so a `burn_in_timecode` posted through
48	        // `rc_export_settings` would vanish without a word and this tool
49	        // would report success on an un-burnt file. It goes to `Exporter`
50	        // beside the settings instead (`RecipeOptions`, `Exporter.export`),
51	        // which is also what reaches GIF and APNG — those never go through
52	        // `ExportWriter` at all.
53	        let options = RecipeOptions(burnInTimecode: try boolArg(a, "burn_in_timecode") ?? false)
54	        let prepared = try onMain {
55	            () throws -> (ProjectDocument, ReelProject, [UInt32: URL], ExportSettings, GraphicSet?)
56	            in
57	            let document = try self.target(a)
58	            guard document.project.duration > 0 else {
59	                throw ToolError(message: "There is nothing on the timeline to export.")
60	            }
61	            // The Range popup of the export sheet, in the sheet's own terms:
62	            // "Whole project" is no override at all, "In/out range" is the
63	            // core's ONE nested `range` object (`export.rs`). The core snaps
64	            // it to the frame grid and clamps it to the project.
65	            var overrides: [String: Any] = [:]
66	            if wholeProject == "in_out" {
67	                guard let range = document.inOutRange, range.end > range.start else {
68	                    throw ToolError(
69	                        message: "This project has no in/out range — set one with set_range "
70	                            + "{start, end}, or export with range \"project\".")
71	                }
72	                overrides["range"] = ["start": range.start, "duration": range.end - range.start]
73	            }
74	            // The sheet's Quality popup, in the core's own words: it resolves
75	            // a tier into these two keys and nothing else
76	            // (`ExportSheetController.overrides()`), so the agent spells them
77	            // the same way rather than re-deriving a rate from a tier name.
78	            // The core validates them — positive, u32 — and an unset key means
79	            // "the preset decides", which is what a nil bitrate already means
80	            // to the writer.
81	            if let video = try self.intArg(a, "video_bitrate") {
82	                overrides["video_bitrate"] = video
83	            }
84	            if let audio = try self.intArg(a, "audio_bitrate") {
85	                overrides["audio_bitrate"] = audio
86	            }
87	            // The sheet's Loudness popup, in the core's words again — and
88	            // through `doubleArg`, not `intArg`: −14.5 LUFS is a real request
89	            // and every one of these figures is a negative fraction. Neither
90	            // is validated here. `export_overrides.rs` owns the bounds
91	            // (−70…0 and −20…0) and the one PAIRING rule among the overrides
92	            // — a `peak_dbtp` with no `loudness_lufs` is refused, because
93	            // normalisation is gain-only and a ceiling with nothing to cap
94	            // would be a key accepted, echoed and silently inert — and it
95	            // names the offending value the way the bitrate refusals do.
96	            // Restating a bound here would be a second spelling of it to
97	            // drift from the first.
98	            // The sheet sends both together and fixes the ceiling at
99	            // −1 dBTP; a caller that wants −0.3 or −2.0 says so here.
100	            if let target = try self.doubleArg(a, "loudness_lufs") {
101	                overrides["loudness_lufs"] = target
102	            }
103	            if let ceiling = try self.doubleArg(a, "peak_dbtp") {
104	                overrides["peak_dbtp"] = ceiling
105	            }
106	            // The sheet's Size popup: a row id, or "Custom…" as an explicit
107	            // [width, height]. Absent is no override at all, so the tool's
108	            // default and the sheet's are one code path in the core — the
109	            // document's size, or an image format's cap.
110	            if let size = try self.exportSizeArg(a, document.project, preset: presetID) {
111	                overrides["width"] = size.width
112	                overrides["height"] = size.height
113	            }
114	            // The sheet's Dynamic Range popup (spec §11 HD-14 (c)), forwarded
115	            // unread: the core's reader and resolver own its three words, its
116	            // per-row defaults and both refusals, each in its own sentence.
117	            if let range = a["dynamic_range"] {
118	                overrides["dynamic_range"] = range
119	            }
120	            // The sheet's Speed popup (spec §11 CX-12 (2)), forwarded unread on the
121	            // same terms: the core reads the three words and refuses a row without one.
122	            if let speed = a["encoder_speed"] {
123	                overrides["encoder_speed"] = speed
124	            }
125	            let settings: ExportSettings
126	            do {
127	                settings = try ReelExport.settings(
128	                    document.project, preset: presetID, overrides: overrides)
129	            } catch {
130	                throw Self.coreRefusal(error)
131	            }
132	            return (
133	                document, document.project, document.mediaURLs(), settings,
134	                GraphicRegistry.shared.snapshot(for: document.recipeKey)
135	            )
136	        }
137	        let (document, project, urls, settings, graphics) = prepared
138	        let url = try Self.requireFolder(
139	            of: Self.destinationURL(path, extension: Exporter.fileExtension(for: settings)))
140	
141	        // The graphics gate, here rather than only in the writer: a module
142	        // that does not compile refuses the CALL, so nothing is queued that
143	        // could only fail (`Exporter.graphicsRefusal`, the writer's own gate).
144	        if let refusal = Exporter.graphicsRefusal(
145	            project: project, settings: settings, graphics: graphics)
146	        {
147	            throw ToolError(message: refusal.localizedDescription)
148	        }
149	        let (id, status) = onMain { () -> (UInt64, String) in
150	            // The editor pauses before its own export so the player is not
151	            // decoding the same media; the agent's does the same.
152	            self.editor(document)?.playback.pause()
153	            let id = ExportQueueController.shared.enqueue(
154	                project: project, urls: urls, settings: settings, to: url, options: options,
155	                graphics: graphics)
156	            AgentExports.shared.track(
157	                id, settings: settings, burnInTimecode: options.burnInTimecode, started: started)
158	            let word = ExportQueueController.shared.job(id).map {
159	                Self.exportStatusWord($0.state)
160	            }
161	            return (id, word ?? "queued")
162	        }
163	        return try jsonResult(["export_id": id, "path": url.path, "status": status])
164	    }

67	    /// **The project handle AND the media URLs are read HERE, at the moment
68	    /// the destination is known, and that is the whole of what makes a queued
69	    /// job immutable.** The handle needs no clone — handles are immutable
70	    /// (spec §5.5) and every edit and undo makes a new one, so this one keeps
71	    /// the timeline as it was confirmed however the document changes, and
72	    /// `Exporter` publishes it on a `RecipeSource` key of its own so even the
73	    /// frames the compositor serves the write come from it. `mediaURLs()` is
74	    /// the half that would otherwise leak: it resolves each bookmark and asks
75	    /// the filesystem whether the file is there, so a job that called it at
76	    /// RUN time would silently pick up a Relink… or a moved file from after it
77	    /// was queued — the exact change an immutable job exists to exclude. A job
78	    /// therefore holds the answer and no document to ask again.

93	        // so this window is the only thing that says it exists.

# core/CLAUDE.md — Rust core rules

Applies to everything under `core/`. Build commands and the FFI three-file
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is
`designs/spec/` (§5 the schemas, §6 the op table, §7 the architecture,
§7.10 this module map in the spec's words; its `README.md` is the index). The long form of
each entry below — why the seam fell where it did — is
`designs/adr/core-file-history.md` (the full history of every cut, with its
line counts, is archived; see its "Original" line); this file is what
governs a module now.

## Module map

- `lib.rs` — module declarations and re-exports only. No implementation code.
- `model.rs` — the spec §5.2 SHAPE: the project, its tracks, clips, sources,
  actions, markers and nests, with the serde defaults that say what an absent
  key means. The struct field names ARE the JSON keys. Nothing else lives here
  but `CanvasOutput` (`Canvas.output`, `sdr` or `hlg`, written only when
  `hlg`, format 23, spec §11 HD-2).
- `model_canvas.rs` — `CanvasBlending` (`Canvas.blending`, `encoded` or
  `linear`, written only when `linear`, format 24, spec §11 GR-18, HD-16),
  re-exported by `model.rs`; the recipe canvas carries it only when linear.
- `model_props.rs` — the schema's VOCABULARY: the per-clip property types
  (`VideoProps`, `AudioProps`, `Crop`, `Shadow`, `ColorAdjust`, `Chroma`,
  `Filter`, `Reflection`, `BlendMode`, `Compressor`, `Duck`) and their
  defaults, re-exported whole by `model.rs` so every `crate::model::X` path
  holds. **`BlendMode`'s, `ObscureKind`'s and `TrackMatte`'s declaration
  ORDER are shader discriminants** (`ProjectSnapshot.swift` and
  `TrackMatte.swift` derive the code from the case index, `Compositor.metal`
  compares against the same integers): append,
  never reorder. `Normal` is 0 with no `+1`, so a zeroed uniform block, an
  older recipe and a file with no `blend` key all render source-over.
- `model_text.rs` · `model_shape.rs` · `model_regions.rs` · `model_motion.rs`
  — the text, shape, region and motion vocabularies, each re-exported through
  `model_props.rs`. Text and shape are the two sources the model only
  DESCRIBES and the platform draws and measures: nothing in either file is
  ever a measured size. Regions (`Spotlight`, `ObscureRegion`, `SpotShape`,
  `MAX_OBSCURE`) share one coordinate frame — the centre as an offset in
  SOURCE pixels from the centre of the layer's cropped rect — which
  `edit_zoom.rs` writes out as an equation and nothing else restates. The
  one load-bearing declaration order in these four is `ObscureKind`'s
  (`model_regions.rs`), a shader discriminant like `BlendMode`'s above;
  elsewhere only the JSON spelling of every variant is, so a rename needs a migration step. The enums are closed:
  there is no neutral kind to fall back to.
- `model_words.rs` — the word-caption vocabulary (format version 9, road
  map 8's W1b): `TextCase`, `Word`, `WordMode`, `ActivePill` and
  `WordStyle` (whose `template()` is what `patch.rs`'s text template walks
  against), re-exported through `model_props.rs`; the FIELDS (`case`,
  `words`, `word_style`) close `TextProps`. Format version 12 (spec §11
  W-12) added three looks as KEYS, each off by default: `ActivePill.glide`,
  `WordStyle.active_fill` and `WordStyle.pause_dim` (0–1, range-checked in
  `props_check.rs`); `Word.end` is read by the recipe since then, not only
  by the pager. It also holds the two facts
  every writer of `text.words` shares, both `pub(crate)` and so named
  directly by their callers (a glob re-export cannot widen them):
  `token_count`, THE token rule (`split_whitespace` — the core is the one
  counter, spec §11 W-2), and `rebase_words`, the one saturating
  subtraction `trim_start`, `roll`, `add_transition`'s handle form and
  `split`'s second half make (W-3). Word times are clip-time POSITIONS: a
  negative start is legal, equal starts are legal, and `snap_animation`
  puts them on the grid after `check_text` has named what the caller sent.
- `model_graphic.rs` — the graphic vocabulary (format version 10, road
  map 10): `GraphicProps` (`name`, `width`, `height`, `in`, `length`,
  `props`) and `GRAPHIC_MIN_SIDE` / `GRAPHIC_MAX_SIDE` and the schema limits
  `GRAPHIC_MAX_PROPS` / `GRAPHIC_MAX_OPTIONS` / `GRAPHIC_MAX_STRING` /
  `GRAPHIC_TYPES` (`GRAPHIC_MAX_SIDE` restates the engine's `MAX_SIDE` and the
  header's `RC_GRAPHIC_MAX_SIDE`, and each other `GRAPHIC_<X>` the engine's
  `<X>`; `tests/graphic_ffi.rs`'s
  `one_max_side_in_the_engine_the_core_and_the_header` and its four
  `one_…_in_the_engine_and_the_core` tests pin them),
  re-exported through `model_props.rs`; the FIELD `Clip.graphic` stays in
  `model.rs`. And the `pub(crate)` checks every writer shares: `check_name`
  (G-3's `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,62}$`, its clause `NAME_RULE` shared with
  `validate`), `check_side`, `check_schema` (the engine's sentences, COPIED —
  no module of the model may name the crate, G-2; a non-boolean `animate`
  on an entry is refused, G-41), `check_props` (by dotted
  path against the schema the op carries, shape only without one; a `null`
  is a removal and is never checked), `check_typed` (one value against its
  entry, answered normalised; `edit_action_graphic.rs` calls it under
  `graphic.props.<key>`), `check_count` (on the map about to be
  STORED). **A props map is changed only by `insert` and
  `shift_remove`**: under `preserve_order`, `Map::remove` is `swap_remove`,
  and `Project ==` cannot see the reorder.
- `model_look.rs` — the look vocabulary (spec §11 GR-7): `Look {kind, amount}`
  (the FIELD `VideoProps.look`, optional, written only when set) and the eight
  built-in looks' definitions as data — Color's four, Light's nine and a split
  tone each — which the recipe's `look` key carries whole, so retuning a look
  is a core change only. `actions.rs` turns a merged look with no valid `kind`
  into `null`, so an action's end can never drop the clip's video group.
  `kind: "lut"` names an imported LUT's media (`media`); `BUILT_IN` is the

  every depth, an array replaces its list, and `null` clears an optional key
  (a required one refuses it). `COMPLETE_ENTRIES` is the one exception to
  "absent keeps": a `video.filters` entry must name both its keys, because a
  list replaces whole and the type's defaults would invent a filter. Nothing
  here is handed a clip or a project: what a patch may carry is a fact about
  the vocabulary, which is `props_check.rs`'s reason for existing one step
  further on. `GROUPS` — every group in its order on `Clip`, the order
  `paste` and a default `paste_attributes` visit them — lives here, its one
  home.

  not about an edit — and it runs BEFORE `edit_props.rs` snaps a patch's
  ticks, which is what lets a refusal name the number the caller sent rather
  than the one a snap rounded it to. Gradient stops are deliberately NOT
  order-checked: a refusal would break dragging one stop past another
  mid-gesture, so the renderer sorts, and the comment says so where the
  check would have gone. A list entry's key names its index —
  `video.filters[0].amount`, `video.obscure[1].x`,
  `shape.gradient.stops[0].color` — so a refusal names the entry as well as
  the field (issue #89).

  and then a count, so a media used by two hundred clips still answers a

  ordered, MERGED — touching as well as overlapping — then cut and closed
  right to left as ONE edit; the singular delegates to it), `lift_range`
  (the hole left open), `close_gap` (refuses rather than closing part way, and
  refuses naming what is there when `at` is on a clip or nothing follows it,

  freeze frame, `shift_clips`, and `locked_track` — THE locked-track
  refusal's sentence, written once here for its three callers
  (`close_gap`, `edit_insert.rs`'s `insert_clip`, `edit_transition.rs`'s
  rippled form), each passing the clause after the comma.
- `edit_edge.rs` · `edit_insert.rs` — the cutting moves that keep something
  fixed on purpose: `slip` and `roll` (a `still` slips the frame it holds;
  any other non-media source is an `Err`; roll's predecessor must end
  EXACTLY at the clip's start); `insert_clip` and `overwrite_clip`,
  compositions of split + insert time + add made ONE op so a drop is one
  undo step and carries the rule neither half states — an insert cuts only
  the destination track and then shifts every unlocked one.

  `trim_start` does; the predecessor's end is an end trim and keeps `length`.
- `edit_transition.rs` — the WRITE half of a transition: `set_transition`,
  `set_transition_duration`, `set_gained_transitions` (a clip that gains an
  overlap gains a transition), `add_transition` (an overlap built from the
  two clips' handles at a hard cut) and `set_transition_style` (curve and

  `add_transition` share (spec §11 #88); `set_transition_duration` refuses on

- `edit_transition_shift.rs` — `add_transition_by_shift`, the `ripple` half
  of `add_transition`: the same overlap made by sliding the incoming clip
  and everything at or after the cut left through `shift_clips`. Cut out of

  a pure move: the handle form spends unused SOURCE and moves nothing,
  this one spends the TIMELINE and moves `close_gap`'s set by `close_gap`'s

  right after the lock check.

  REMOVES at every depth rather than clearing, and `patch.rs`'s walk and
  read per group. The door is composed here because which groups an end
  patch names, and what a `null` in one means, are facts about an ACTION;

  and a non-object group slot is replaced by `{}`, never indexed. `set_action`

  `parse_payload` are `pub(crate)`, because `edit_paste_attributes.rs` reads
  the same payload.
  `graphic` in a `patch` is `edit_action_graphic.rs`'s arm, read against
  the op's `schema` after the three groups' walk (G-34); in an `off` path it

  integrals of `actions.rs`'s curves), `is_ramped` (media clips only),
  `end_speed`'s clamp, `peak_rate` (the greatest rate the clip NAMES, its
  base and every end rate, the ×12 figure, SR-19 (d)), `source_at`, `rate_at`,
  `rate_in_force` (what `clip_state`'s top-level `speed` answers, SR-21); `of_length` (the

  actions, SR-18 (a)), `time_for_source` (its inverse) and `head_end_rate`

  edges, and `RATE_SAMPLES` + 1 samples across a ramp piece, SR-26).
- `speed_segments.rs` — the map cut into plan pieces: `Held` at one rate
  (an equal-rate action is held), `Ramp` one video segment per canvas
  frame, and the ramp audio map with a breakpoint every 600 ticks;
  `constant_ramp_audio` is the two-point map, flagged `constant`, that
  `evaluate.rs` puts on a constant Keep pitch off time-scaled audio segment
  so Swift renders it as a ramp's (SR-28).
  `Project::source_map` (SR-20) answers a media clip's source map: a ramped
  clip its ramp audio map, byte-equal to the plan segment's `ramp.map`, a
  constant clip its two points, flagged `ramped` as `is_ramped` is; a
  ramped clip's answer also carries `rate`, `rate_profile`'s list (SR-26),

- `edit_action_speed.rs` — `set_action_end`'s speed arm and the overrun
  refusals R1/R2/R3 for `set_action_end`, `set_action` and
  `remove_action`: a ramp that would read past the media's end is refused,
  naming the largest end rate that fits (floored to 0.001,
  `largest_fitting_end_rate`, which split's eased tail also uses, over the
  shared `largest_fitting_rate` that `add_speed_ramp` also solves through).
- `edit_action_ramp.rs` — `add_speed_ramp`, the ramp presets (SR-23, #340):
  Ramp Up, Ramp Down, Speed Dip or Speed Burst as ordinary Speed actions in
  one step, in clip time over `[from, to)` or the whole clip, from the BASE
  `rate_in_force` at `from`; Up and Burst need a rate above it, Down and Dip
  one below. An action anywhere in the span (a dip's hold gap included) is
  refused by name, never replaced, and a preset that would read past the
  media's end is refused naming the rate that fits.
- `edit_action_graphic.rs` — `set_action_end`'s graphic arm (G-34):
  `read_graphic_end` checks the patch's `graphic.props` (never the stored
  end's) against the op's `schema` through `check_typed` under
  `graphic.props.<key>`, discards a `kinds`, refuses a prop its module
  marks `animate: false` (G-41), an undeclared prop, a layer key and a
  missing schema by name (an asset is an ordinary switch, `""` naming no
  image, G-42), and answers each prop's kind and the default for each the
  clip lacks (`schema_default`; an asset's is its string default or `""`); `write_graphic_end` stores `props` and `kinds` by

- `edit_paste_attributes.rs` — `paste_attributes`, cut out of `edit_paste.rs`
  under the size rule as a pure move ahead of spec §11 G-32: the payload's
  EARLIEST clip's property groups (then the front-most, then the lower id —
  never the array's first) copied onto each target, replaced whole and never
  merged. `PasteGroup` is the five names it takes — the four patch groups and
  `graphic`, which is never in the default set: a graphic's `props` copied
  whole onto clips drawn by the SAME module, the target keeping its name,
  size, `in` and `length`, written with `insert` and `shift_remove`
  (`model_graphic.rs`'s rule). A target key the payload lacks that an
  action on the target names (`names_prop`) is kept (G-34 (d), amending
  G-32 (e)). `skip_missing` drops a named group the payload
  clip lacks and skips a target that cannot take one. **The copied props are
  shape-checked once, the first time a target takes them**: a paste nothing
  takes never reads the map. `patch::Group` gains no variant for it.
- `edit_zoom.rs` — `add_zoom_action`, the screencast zoom, and `ZoomRegion`,
  the one op ARGUMENT that is a caller-authored object: its `Deserialize` is
  written out rather than derived so it answers as a patch does — an object
  required (a list is not read member by member), an unknown or missing
  member named, a wrong-typed one named by its path. **Its module doc
  IS the placement equation** between the region frame and canvas pixels,
  rotation and crop included; it composes `add_action` + `set_action` +
  `set_action_end` so a drag is one undo step and every refusal is inherited.
- `edit_adjustment.rs` — `Source::Adjustment`'s rules (spec §11 GR-6):
  `add_adjustment_clip`, and the refusals every other door asks it for — a
  transition (from `add_transition`, `set_transition`, `set_transition_style`
  and the overlap rule), a nest, and the blur, sharpen and pixelate filters
  and any blend mode. The recipe draws it as `{"kind":"adjustment"}` (plus its `qualifier` when

  matte track it is dropped before the frame's mattes (inert).
- `edit_background.rs` — `add_background` and `add_blurred_background`: one
  clip on a NEW back-most track, OPS rather than app-side composites because
  the composite carries constraints no half states. A blurred copy drops
  `enabled.audio`, `audio.duck`, the transition, the actions and the label
  (each a wrong picture or a wrong sound if carried) and refuses a nest.
  Default plate colour is white: the canvas is already black.
- `actions.rs` — action evaluation and interpolation, and `clip_state`
  (with a top-level `speed`, `speed_map.rs`'s rate in force, the inspector's
  Rate inside an action, SR-21);
  `video_json` / `color_json` write all thirteen colour keys, the tone keys at
  0 included, for the five callers that must see them (the base state,
  `clip_state`, `patch.rs`'s template, `recipe_layer.rs`, `edit_split.rs`);
  its last line of defence is `actions_clamp.rs`'s, and a graphic's props
  are `actions_graphic.rs`'s (spec §11 G-34), carried in `Evaluated.graphic`
  and `clip_state`'s `graphic`. **The LIST rule is stated here once as the
  crate's**: an end patch interpolates a list per index when the lengths
  match and each pair of entries agrees on its discrete fields (`kind`,
  `shape`), and switches at the end otherwise; `video.filters` and `video.obscure` are both governed by it and carry no code of their own.
- `actions_clamp.rs` — `clamp_video`, `clamp_audio` and `clamp_text`, the
  evaluator's last line of defence (`set_action_end` checks a `video`,
  `audio` or `text` end patch's keys and kinds but deliberately not its
  VALUES, and never looks at the clip for them; this bounds every value
  such a patch can carry and forces `normal` on a nest clip), with
  `bounded` / `finite_or`; the first two a pure move out of `actions.rs`

- `actions_curves.rs` — `curves_json` (all six curves, an absent one
  as its domain's identity, for `video_json`'s callers),
  `align_identity_curves` (spec §11 GR-12, GR-32: an identity curve
  meeting a curve of another count in an action takes that curve's x's,
  its ends at 0 and 1 on a tone curve and every value the neutral on a
  hue curve, so a grade animates from neutral), and `CurveBlend`,
  `curve_blends` and `blended_curves_json` (spec §11 GR-34: two

  curve and the eased t in `Evaluated.curve_blends`, and only the recipe
  layer and `clip_state` write it, as `{from, to, t}`; never a file).
- `actions_qualifier.rs` — `qualifier_json` (spec §11 GR-35): a qualifier
  with its `blur` present even at 0, which `actions.rs`'s `video_json` writes
  for a non-neutral one so the blur animates from 0; and `align_hue_center`
  (spec §11 GR-13): before
  the lerp, an action's target hue centre moves by ±360 when the two
  centres are more than 180° apart, so the centre animates the short
  way round (350 → 10 through 0); `clamp_qualifier` brings it back
  into [0, 360).
- `actions_color.rs` — `blend_colors` (spec §11 G-43): after the spanning
  action's `lerp`, each of the model's colours — `COLOR_POINTERS`' eight
  `[r, g, b, a]` in `video` and `text` and `CHROMA_KEY_POINTER`'s `[r, g,

  action's two ends (`oklab_mix_unit` / `oklab_mix_rgb`), only strictly
  inside the action and only where the ends differ, so an untouched colour
  stays exact; an end of the wrong arity keeps §5.4's hold-then-switch.
- `actions_graphic.rs` — a graphic clip's props at a clip time (format
  version 13, spec §11 G-34): finished actions' `end.graphic.props` laid
  over the clip's map by `insert`, the spanning one interpolated — a number
  in floating point, never rounded; a `color` (by `end.graphic.kinds`,
  never by shape) in OKLab with straight alpha through `model_color.rs`'s

  with no start, held and switched at the end. Total. `names_prop` is
  `set_graphic`'s and `paste_attributes`' question.
- `transition.rs` — overlap detection, THE overlap rule (spec §11), eased
  progress at *t*. An overlap with no kind still dissolves
  (`unwrap_or_default`), and `add_clip` onto an overlap mints a
  `cross_dissolve`, so a no-transition baseline is built by moving clips
  apart, not by clearing the kind.
- `transition_search.rs` — the bounded fitting arithmetic for both hard-cut
  transition forms: the old handle decrement path by total, and exact
  forbidden shift intervals across fixed/moved clips for ripple, counted in
  whole grid frames back from the cut (`time::frames_within`). It does
  not enumerate timeline frames; final placements still pass
  `check_overlap_rule`.
- `evaluate.rs` — the A/B assignment, `assign()`, that the plan and the
  recipe share, and `drawing_instances`, which both the instruction tiling
  and the layer list are built from. `assign` leaves a clip's audio out above

  the same stored numbers Swift's `SpeedAudioDrop.peakSpeed` reads.
- `plan.rs` — `composition_plan()` (spec §7.2): the plan's JSON from
  `assign()`, the instruction tiling, and the decoder-budget warning
  (`MAX_CONCURRENT_VIDEO_TRACKS`). Deterministic to the byte. A pure move
  out of `evaluate.rs` (grading GR1).
